But the relief is significant for the pharma sector in the stock market. It is the only sector that has been resilient in the recent fall and has clearly outperformed in last one year.
While Sensex has lost 13%, Nifty pharma index has gained 18% this year.
In FY26, India’s total pharma exports rose to $31.1 billion. Of these, exports to the US stood at $9.47 billion. US share of India’s pharma exports stand at 30.4%.
Firms such as Sun Pharma, Dr Reddy’s and Cipla are engaged in the production and sale of rare disease & specialty therapies. Sun Pharma and Cipla sell infertility treatments drugs. Biocon and Cipla are involved in drugs for cell & gene therapies. Zydus Life and Hester Bio deal in animal pharmaceuticals.
ALSO READ: Dr. Reddy’s, Lupin shares among buzzing stocks as pharma sector back in focus
Which drugs are covered?
The US Commerce Department’s notice provides a zero-tariff exemption for a select group of specialised pharmaceutical and medical products. The list includes medicines used to treat rare diseases and infertility, as well as cell and gene therapies, antibody-drug conjugates and veterinary pharmaceuticals.
The exemption also extends to components used in the manufacture of these products. However, the measure is narrowly focused on speciality medicines and does not apply to the pharmaceutical sector as a whole.
Eligible products include medicines for which all approved indications relate to orphan or rare diseases. The zero-tariff category also covers nuclear medicines, plasma-derived therapies and fertility treatments.
Certain medical countermeasures designed to address chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear threats are also included in the exemption.
India among 20 eligible jurisdictions
India is among 20 countries and jurisdictions whose qualifying pharmaceutical products can benefit from the zero-tariff treatment. The list also includes Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, the European Union, Guatemala, Indonesia, Japan, Jordan, Malaysia, North Macedonia, South Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Taiwan, Thailand, the UK and Vietnam.
According to the notice, qualifying products originating from these jurisdictions may receive a zero per cent tariff because the countries have existing or forthcoming trade and security framework agreements with the US.
The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security has also retained the flexibility to extend the exemption to products that it determines are necessary to address an urgent healthcare need in the US.

input.title: Sun Pharma Inks Global Lerodalcibep Deal, Gets Rights Outside US, China
input.content:
Sun Pharma Inks Global Lerodalcibep Deal, Gets Rights Outside US, China
Mumbai: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Sun Pharma) and LIB Therapeutics Inc. (LIB) have entered into an exclusive licensing agreement granting Sun Pharma rights to commercialize and manufacture lerodalcibep worldwide, excluding the United States and China.
Lerodalcibep, marketed as Lyrokaul in the European Union, is a once-monthly PCSK9 inhibitor for lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). It received European Union approval on September 21, 2026.
The agreement strengthens Sun Pharma's Innovative Medicines portfolio through access to the PCSK9 inhibitor market outside the United States and China, which was valued at US$3.7 billion in the period ending Q2 2026 and grew at a 38% compound annual growth rate over the preceding two years, according to IQVIA. The global PCSK9 market is approaching US$7 billion in 2026.
Under the agreement, LIB Therapeutics will receive an upfront payment and future milestone payments, together with royalties based on net sales in the licensed territories. Other terms of the agreement are confidential.
Lerodalcibep is approved in the EU under the brand name Lyrokaul for the treatment of adult patients with hypercholesterolaemia and mixed dyslipidaemia.
In the United States, lerodalcibep is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration under the brand name Lerochol as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce LDL-C in adults with hypercholesterolaemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HeFH).
The partnership is intended to address a significant unmet need in cardiovascular care. According to the companies, many patients at high or very high cardiovascular risk remain above recently updated and more globally harmonized 2026 guideline-recommended LDL-C goals despite treatment.
In the DA VINCI observational study across 18 European countries, 33% of patients assessed on stable oral lipid-lowering therapy achieved their risk-based 2019 European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society (ESC/EAS) LDL-C goals. The 2019 goals were applied retrospectively to data collected in 2017-2018, and the 33% figure relates to patients assessed on stable therapy.
Treatment guidelines now emphasize both additional LDL-C reductions and lower targets for patients at high and very high cardiovascular risk, with additional therapies recommended when statins alone are insufficient. PCSK9 inhibitors provide an additional treatment option for achieving these LDL-C goals.
The companies said the gap between treatment goals and real-world control highlights an opportunity to broaden access to lipid-lowering treatment across Europe and Sun Pharma's worldwide licensed markets.
“Once-monthly lerodalcibep dosing, with robust LDL-C reduction and the added benefits of a small-volume injection and six-month ambient storage, simplifies treatment for patients and offers greater convenience,” said Kirti W Ganorkar, Managing Director of Sun Pharma.
“This agreement marks a significant step in strengthening our global Innovative Medicines portfolio, particularly in cardiovascular care. With exclusive rights outside the United States and China, we look forward to expanding access to this important treatment option for patients globally,” Ganorkar added.
Evan Stein, MD, PhD, Chief Operating and Scientific Officer and co-founder of LIB Therapeutics, said, “LIB is extremely pleased to partner with Sun Pharma, a well-established global pharmaceutical company with a growing focus on innovative medicines.”
“Sun Pharma’s international presence and experience in building global innovative brands make it an ideal partner to bring lerodalcibep to more patients. Together, we aim to expand access for patients with cardiovascular disease, or at high cardiovascular risk, who need substantial additional LDL-cholesterol reductions despite existing treatment,” Stein added.
According to IQVIA, the PCSK9 inhibitor market outside the United States and China reached US$3.7 billion in the period ending Q2 2026 (MAT Q2 2026), growing at a 38% CAGR over the preceding two years. Europe alone accounted for a US$2.9 billion PCSK9 inhibitor market in MAT Q2 2026.
Sun Pharma will be responsible for pursuing regulatory approvals in licensed territories where approval has not yet been obtained.
Lerodalcibep is a novel antibody-mimetic biologic and recombinant fusion protein that inhibits proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). It is designed to deliver sustained reductions in LDL-C, often referred to as “bad” cholesterol.
The drug is administered as a once-monthly 300 mg/1.2 mL subcutaneous injection.
Lerodalcibep has received marketing authorization from the European Medicines Agency under the brand name Lyrokaul. The EU label permits storage in the original carton at room temperature up to 25°C for up to six months after removal from refrigeration, offering flexibility for patients at home and while travelling.
In the United States, lerodalcibep is approved by the US FDA under the brand name Lerochol in both autoinjector and prefilled-syringe presentations.
Therapeutic Indications
Lyrokaul is indicated in adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HeFH) and nonfamilial hypercholesterolaemia, or mixed dyslipidaemia, as an adjunct to diet:
in combination with a statin or a statin with other lipid-lowering therapies in patients unable to reach LDL-C goals with the maximum tolerated dose of a statin; or
alone or in combination with other lipid-lowering therapies in patients who are statin intolerant or for whom a statin is contraindicated.
Contraindications
Lyrokaul is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to the active substance or any of the excipients listed in the package leaflet.
Special Warnings and Precautions
Traceability: To improve the traceability of biological medicinal products, the name and batch number of the administered product should be clearly recorded.
Sodium: Lyrokaul contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per dose and is therefore essentially “sodium-free.”
Polysorbate 80: The medicinal product contains 0.24 mg polysorbate 80 (E 433) per dose. Polysorbates may cause allergic reactions.
Renal impairment: Lyrokaul should be used with caution in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease. The medicine has not been studied in these populations.
Severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease: Lyrokaul has not been studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease. It should only be used in these patients if the anticipated clinical benefit outweighs the risk.
Drug Interactions
No interaction studies have been performed.
Fertility, Pregnancy and Lactation
Pregnancy: There are no data from the use of lerodalcibep in pregnant women. Animal studies do not indicate direct or indirect harmful effects with respect to reproductive toxicity. As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of Lyrokaul during pregnancy.
Breast-feeding: It is unknown whether lerodalcibep is excreted in human milk. Available pharmacodynamic and toxicological data in animals have shown excretion of lerodalcibep in milk. A risk to newborns and infants cannot be excluded.
A decision must be made whether to discontinue breast-feeding or to discontinue or abstain from Lyrokaul therapy, taking into account the benefit of breast-feeding for the child and the benefit of therapy for the woman.
Fertility: No data are available on the effect of lerodalcibep on human fertility. Animal fertility studies were not performed; however, no effects were seen on surrogate markers of fertility in animal studies.
Effects on Driving and Use of Machines
Lyrokaul has no or negligible influence on the ability to drive and use machines.
Adverse Reactions
The most frequently reported adverse reactions in patients treated with lerodalcibep are injection-site reaction (6.7%), injection-site erythema (3.6%) and injection-site bruising (1.6%).
Injection-site reactions occurred in 11.6% of patients treated with lerodalcibep in pivotal studies. The most frequently occurring reactions were injection-site reaction (6.7%), injection-site erythema (3.6%), injection-site pruritis (1.0%) and injection-site bruising (1.6%).
The proportion of patients who discontinued treatment due to injection-site reactions was 1.0%. Adverse reactions were generally mild or moderate in severity. Severe injection-site reactions occurred in 0.2% of cases, were transient and resolved without leading to discontinuation of the study drug.
Immunogenicity
Anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses, including neutralising antibodies (NAb), were low-titer and did not appear to have a clinically meaningful impact on the efficacy or safety of lerodalcibep, except for a higher rate of injection-site reactions in patients with treatment-emergent ADA compared with patients who were ADA-negative.
The excluded China territory comprises mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.
Worldwide rights under the agreement exclude the United States and China. Certain other excluded territories, limited in number, will be covered through separate agreements between Sun Pharma and LIB.
LIB Therapeutics Inc. is a privately held, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel therapies for patients with cardiovascular disease and familial hypercholesterolaemia to help them achieve their LDL-C goals.
LIB was advised and assisted by Greenhill & Co investment bank UK.

input.title: Lilly widens lead over Sun Pharma in anti-baldness contest with paediatric approval
input.content:

Lilly widens lead over Sun Pharma in anti-baldness contest with paediatric approval
                    The latest approval builds on the drug’s established use and opens a new market for the company, presently insulated with Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi which is currently approved only for adults.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Indianapolis: US pharma giant Eli Lilly has secured marketing approval for Olumiant (baricitinib), a once-daily pill, for the treatment of pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with severe alopecia areata (AA). 
The latest approval builds on the drug’s established use and opens a new market for the company, presently insulated with other rivals particularly, Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi which is currently approved only for adults.
AA is a chronic immune-mediated disease that causes unpredictable hair loss
Under its pivotal Phase 3 study (BRAVE-AA-PEDS) 42 per cent of patients receiving the 4 mg dose of Olumiant achieved at least 80 per cent scalp hair coverage, while 90 per cent or more scalp hair coverage was observed in patients receiving the 2 mg dose, as measured by the SALT score, a standardised measure of scalp hair loss.
According to Lilly, for teenagers, the recommended dose is 2 mg once daily, which may be increased to 4 mg daily if the treatment response is inadequate.
Meanwhile for the new patient group, Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi is currently undergoing an investigator-led trial in the US. The company has not provided guidance on the stage of development and expected approval timeline.
Leqselvi is taken twice daily, compared with a once-daily regimen for Lilly’s Olumiant, and is available in a higher dose ceiling of 8 mg.
According to the company, as of June, Leqselvi had surpassed 1,000 prescribers in the US and has reported "positive uptake" across the country.

input.title: Nykaa Wanderlust enters microdrama space with ‘Hotel Wanderlust’
input.content:
Nykaa and independent creative agency SW Network have launched ‘Hotel Wanderlust’, a six-episode microdrama series for Nykaa Wanderlust, the brand’s experiential bath and body care range.
Set in a fictional hotel, the series stars comedian and actor Varun Thakur and Shachi, who plays a receptionist with a set of quirks. Each episode features a new guest, including creators Srishti Garg, Pulkit Kochar and Mishall B, as they navigate different everyday situations.
Nykaa Wanderlust’s products, including body mists, perfumes, shower gels and lotions, are integrated into the episodes as part of the storyline rather than being presented through standalone advertising breaks.
According to SW Network, the series has clocked close to a million views across its six episodes within two weeks of launch. The agency says the format was developed using audience research and storytelling techniques tailored to short-form content.
Himani Mangtani, business head, SW Network, said, “Social media is changing how people consume stories, and brands need to evolve with it. Hotel Wanderlust allowed us to build a format that feels native to the platform while giving Nykaa Wanderlust a distinctive world to play in. It’s also a reminder that when passionate people come together around a strong idea, great things can happen.”
Vinit Patil, creative director, SW Network, said, “Microdrama has its own grammar, and we learned how to speak it. It’s about giving people a reason to stop, then a reason to stay, and finally a reason to share. That means putting the drama before an expensive production spectacle, and investing in the story, character arcs, popular faces and distribution that can make the story travel. With Hotel Wanderlust, that thinking shaped every beat.”
Omna Winston, creative head, Nykaa, said, “Gen Z doesn’t want brands to just talk to them; they want brands to create experiences they can be part of. Hotel Wanderlust was born from that thought. We wanted to take the travel-inspired world of Nykaa Wanderlust and turn it into a format that feels native to Instagram, bite-sized, entertaining and full of personality. The products are woven into that world naturally, making the brand part of the experience rather than an interruption.”
With all six episodes now available, the series also supports the launch of Nykaa Wanderlust’s new fragrance line. The campaign marks SW Network’s focus on content-led and platform-first brand storytelling.

input.title: Sun Pharma steps into PCSK9 arena with LIB Therapeutics’ monthly-shot
input.content:
- Pharma Industry
- 3 min read
Sun Pharma steps into PCSK9 arena with LIB Therapeutics’ monthly-shot
                    The exclusive licensing agreement opens up a potential $3.7 billion market opportunity for Sun Pharma and gives room to expand the base of its specialty sales in new geographies. Presently the market is populated with several established players such as Novartis and Amgen, and a new wave of oral pills from Merck and AstraZeneca is set to add another layer of competition.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Mumbai: Indian Pharma major, Sun Pharmaceuticals Industries has announced to have acquired exclusive rights to manufacture and market (in ex-US sand China market) a novel PCSK9 inhibitor, Lyrokaul (lerodalcibep) from US-based LIB Therapeutics.
The once-monthly injection is approved in the US and Europe to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), often referred to as “bad” cholesterol, in adults with hypercholesterolemia.
Under the agreement, LIB will receive an undisclosed upfront payment, future milestone payments and royalties based on net sales in the licensed territories.
Other terms of the agreement were not disclosed, citing confidentiality. Sun Pharma will be responsible for pursuing regulatory approvals in licensed territories where the drug has not yet been approved.
“Once-monthly lerodalcibep dosing, with robust LDL-C reduction and the added benefits of a small-volume injection and six-month ambient storage, simplifies treatment for patients and offers greater convenience”, said Kirti W Ganorkar, Managing Director of Sun Pharma.
“We aim to expand access for patients with cardiovascular disease, or at high cardiovascular risk, who need substantial additional LDL-cholesterol reductions despite existing treatment,” added, Evan Stein, co-founder, LIB Therapeutics.
Notably, PCSK9 inhibitors have opened a new frontier in cardiovascular risk management, particularly for patients who do not achieve adequate LDL-C reduction with statins alone and remain at elevated risk of heart attacks and strokes.
Lerodalcibep, branded as Lyrokaul is a antibody-mimetic biologic and recombinant fusion protein that works by binding and blocking the PCSK9 protein in the blood to prevent it from destroying LDL receptors to improve the absorption of bad cholesterol in the liver.
Under trials, the drug has demonstrated up to 62 per cent reduction in LDL-C levels compared with placebo.
The latest buyout opens a potential $3.7 billion market opportunity which is further growing at a 38 per cent CAGR over the past two years, according to IQVIA estimates.
In the highly competitive PCSK9 inhibitor market, Mumbai-based Sun Pharma will lock horns with established rivals such as Novartis and Amgen, as well as the other emerging competition from oral therapies developed by Merck and AstraZeneca.
Against Amgen’s Repatha (evolocumab), Lyrokaul did not demonstrate (LIBerate-HoFH trial) non-inferiority, with an average reduction in LDL-C levels of 4.9 per cent compared with 10.3 per cent after 24 weeks of treatment. This represented a 5.4 percentage-point difference, against the prespecified non-inferiority margin of 6 percentage points.
Its other competitors include Novartis’ inclisiran, marketed as Leqvio, which is administered twice during the first three months, followed by a six-month dosing schedule.
However, in the US, the monthly injection is available in both autoinjector and prefilled-syringe (PFS) formats, enabling self-administration and potentially reducing the need for frequent healthcare visits compared with Leqvio.
Adding to the competitive landscape are daily-pills such as Lipfendra (enlicitide) of Merck and AstraZeneca’s laroprovstat (under development) which are seeking to challenge the established injectable model with the convenience of oral dosing.
The licensing pact broadens the scope of Sun Pharma’s specialty portfolio, traditionally anchored in dermatology, ophthalmology and onco therapeutic areas. It also expands the company’s geographic breakup, as the US currently accounts for nearly 85 per cent of its total specialty sales.
However, investors remain cautious about the potential margin upside, amid the growing scrutiny of such deals to deliver meaningful accretion to earnings.
Sun Pharma’s stock was down 0.4 per cent at Rs 1,843 on the NSE at 12 p.m.

input.title: Sun Pharma in focus after tapping into $3.7 Billion ex-US/China PCSK9 inhibitor market
input.content:
High cholesterol is one of those problems that most people know about and far fewer manage well. Statins are the first line of defence, but many patients at high cardiovascular risk still cannot bring their LDL cholesterol down to the levels doctors want. That gap has opened the door for newer injectable therapies. For drug makers, it has also become a race to find the right products and the right partners to take them to patients in every region.
Shares of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. were trading at Rs. 1,844.20, down 0.43 percent from previous close of Rs. 1,852.20. The stock opened at Rs. 1,844,.00, reaching an intraday high of Rs. 1,855.00 and low of Rs. 1,839.10. The company currently has a market capitalization of Rs. 4,42,389 crores.
What's the News?
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has signed an exclusive licensing agreement with US-based LIB Therapeutics for lerodalcibep, a PCSK9 inhibitor that lowers LDL cholesterol. Sun Pharma gets the rights to commercialise and manufacture the drug worldwide, except in the United States and China. LIB will receive an upfront payment, milestone payments and royalties on net sales in the licensed territories. The other terms are confidential.
The timing works well for the Sun. The drug received European approval on 21 September under the brand name Lyrokaul, and it is already approved in the US as Lerochol. It is a once-monthly injection, and the EU label allows patients to keep it at room temperature for up to six months after taking it out of the fridge. Sun will handle regulatory approvals in any licensed market where the drug is not yet cleared. Managing Director Kirti Ganorkar called it a significant step in building the company's global innovative medicines portfolio, especially in cardiovascular care.
Business Analysis
Looking at the quarterly results of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., the company’s consolidated revenue increased by 11.92 percent YoY, from Rs. 14,315.8 crore in Q1 FY26 to Rs. 16,023.5 crore in Q1 FY27, and increased by 6.33 percent QoQ from Rs. 15,070.2 crore in Q4 FY26.
In Q1 FY27 Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.’s consolidated net profit increased by 27.04 percent YoY, reaching Rs. 2,894.79 crore compared to Rs. 2,278.63 crore during the same period last year. As compared to Q4 FY26, the net profit has increased by 6.66 percent, from Rs. 2,714.03 crore.
The basic earnings per share stood at Rs. 12.1 as against Rs. 9.5 recorded in the same quarter in the previous year, FY2026.
Sun Pharma is best known for its generics and its position as India's largest pharmaceutical company. But its innovative medicines business, which covers dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology, is the part it is pushing hardest. That portfolio already contributes about 22% of company sales. Adding a cardiovascular product gives it a new therapy area beyond skin and eye care, which reduces its reliance on a few categories.
The structure of the deal also suits Sun. Rather than spending years on discovery and trials, it is licensing a drug that already has approvals and paying through milestones and royalties. That keeps the upfront risk lower and ties later payments to how well the drug sells. Sun's existing reach in more than 100 countries and its experience in building specialty brands should help it move quickly in Europe and other markets. Since this is a licensing deal, there is no order book to speak of. What matters is how fast approvals come through and how well the launches go.
Industry Context
The market for PCSK9 inhibitors is growing fast. According to IQVIA, sales outside the US and China reached $3.7 billion in the year to the second quarter of 2026, growing at a 38% annual rate over the previous two years. Europe alone accounted for $2.9 billion of that. Globally, the market is close to $7 billion this year, so the territories Sun now controls make up more than half of it.
Demand is being driven by a large treatment gap. In a European study covering 18 countries, only 33% of patients on stable oral lipid-lowering therapy reached their risk-based LDL cholesterol goals. Updated 2026 guidelines now push for lower targets in high-risk patients, and that makes add-on therapies more relevant. Easier dosing and storage can also help more patients stay on treatment, and that is where a once-monthly injection with room-temperature flexibility has an edge.
Company Overview
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited is the largest pharmaceutical company in India and a leading generics player in the US and in emerging markets. It operates across innovative medicines, generics and consumer healthcare, and its medicines reach physicians and patients in over 100 countries. Its vertically integrated operations run manufacturing facilities across five continents. The company's workforce is drawn from more than 50 nations.

input.title: Sun Pharma bags rights to $3.7 billion cholesterol drug market globally
input.content:
Sun Pharma bags rights to $3.7 billion cholesterol drug market globally
Sun Pharma will commercialise and manufacture LIB Therapeutics' once-monthly cholesterol drug outside the US and China after its EU approval
Listen to This Article
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has signed a global licensing deal with US-based LIB Therapeutics for Lerodalcibep, a once-monthly drug used to lower “bad” cholesterol, giving it exclusive rights to commercialise and manufacture the medicine outside the US and China, the company said in an exchange filing on Monday.
 
The deal gives Sun Pharma access to a $3.7 billion market for PCSK9 inhibitors, a class of cholesterol-lowering medicines. The market outside the US and China grew at a compound annual growth rate of 38 per cent over the two years to June 2026, according to IQVIA data cited by the companies. Europe alone accounted for $2.9 billion of the market.
 
The agreement comes days after the European Union approved Lerodalcibep under the brand name Lyrokaul. The drug was approved on September 21 for adults with high cholesterol and mixed dyslipidaemia.
 
Under the deal, LIB Therapeutics will receive an upfront payment, milestone payments and royalties based on sales in Sun Pharma’s licensed markets. The companies have not disclosed the financial terms. Sun Pharma will also seek regulatory approvals in markets where the drug is not yet approved.
 
What is Lerodalcibep?
Lerodalcibep is a PCSK9 inhibitor that reduces levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), commonly known as bad cholesterol. It is given once a month through a 300 mg injection under the skin.
Also Read
Its EU approval covers adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia, including inherited high cholesterol, and mixed dyslipidaemia. It can be used with a statin when patients do not reach their LDL-C targets, or on its own or with other cholesterol-lowering medicines when statins cannot be used.
 
One feature that could make the drug easier to use is its storage requirement. In the EU, Lyrokaul can be kept at room temperature of up to 25 degrees Celsius for six months after being removed from refrigeration.
 
Lerodalcibep is already approved in the US under the brand name Lerochol. The US market, however, is not part of Sun Pharma’s agreement, and neither is China.
Why the market matters
The companies said the deal addresses a gap in cholesterol treatment. Despite existing medicines, many high-risk patients do not reach recommended LDL-C levels. A European observational study cited in the release found that only 33 per cent of patients assessed on stable oral lipid-lowering treatment had reached their risk-based LDL-C goals.
 
“This agreement marks a significant step in strengthening our global Innovative Medicines portfolio, particularly in cardiovascular care. With exclusive rights outside the United States and China, we look forward to expanding access to this important treatment option for patients globally,” said Kirti W Ganorkar, managing director, Sun Pharma.
“Once-monthly” dosing and the ability to store the medicine at room temperature for six months could also make the treatment more convenient for patients, the company said.
 
Sun Pharma will now be responsible for commercialising the drug in its licensed territories and pursuing approvals where required. LIB Therapeutics will continue to receive payments linked to the drug’s development and sales.
 
“Sun Pharma’s international presence and experience in building global innovative brands make it an ideal partner to bring Lerodalcibep to more patients. Together, we aim to expand access for patients with cardiovascular disease, or at high cardiovascular risk, who need substantial additional LDL-cholesterol reductions despite existing treatment,” said Evan Stein, chief operating and scientific officer and co-founder of LIB Therapeutics.

input.title: Sun Pharma Obtains Global Ex-US And China Rights For Lerodalcibep
input.content:
Sun Pharma Obtains Global Ex-US And China Rights For Lerodalcibep
- **Exclusive Licensing:** Sun Pharma secures global rights (excluding the US and China) to commercialize and manufacture Lerodalcibep from LIB Therapeutics. - **Strategic Therapeutics:** Lerodalcibep is a once-monthly PCSK9 inhibitor designed to lower LDL-C ('bad' cholesterol) and has recently received EU approval on September 21, 2026. - **Market Opportunity:** The partnership positions Sun Pharma to tap into a US$3.7 billion ex-US and China PCSK9 market growing at 38% CAGR. - **Commercial Terms:** LIB Therapeutics is slated to receive upfront and future milestone payments, alongside sales royalties.
Market snapshot: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has entered into an exclusive licensing agreement with US-based LIB Therapeutics Inc. to commercialize and manufacture its novel cholesterol-lowering drug, Lerodalcibep, globally excluding the US and China. This strategic move directly strengthens Sun Pharma's Innovative Medicines portfolio and grants it entry into a rapidly growing cardiovascular therapy segment.
Data Snapshot
- The ex-US and China market for PCSK9 inhibitors is estimated at US$3.7 billion, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 38%.
- The global PCSK9 inhibitor market is approaching US$7 billion in 2026.
- Lerodalcibep received European Union regulatory approval on September 21, 2026, under the brand name Lyrokaul.
Key Takeaways
- The licensing of Lerodalcibep advances Sun Pharma’s strategy to shift from low-margin generics to higher-value specialty brand molecules.
- Approved as Lyrokaul in the EU, the drug offers clinical differentiation with its once-monthly subcutaneous dose and unique 6-month ambient temperature storage.
- Lerodalcibep targets high-risk cardiovascular patients whose bad cholesterol (LDL-C) remains poorly controlled by standard oral therapies.
- The licensing terms minimize massive upfront capital layout by utilizing milestone-based payments and sales-based royalties.
SAHI Perspective
This licensing deal illustrates Sun Pharma's continued tactical pivot away from the highly competitive US generics market towards the lucrative, high-barrier global innovative specialty space. By opting for a regional exclusive licensing model (excluding the US and China, where clinical trials and commercial entry are prohibitively expensive), Sun Pharma leverages its formidable manufacturing capabilities and distribution footprint in Europe, India, and emerging markets. This asset-light approach, backed by Lerodalcibep's recent European approval, represents a lower-risk entry into the multi-billion-dollar global PCSK9 segment.
Market Implications
The acquisition of these rights is expected to be positively received by the market as it strengthens the company's long-term pipeline of high-margin specialty products. It supports the company's existing Global Specialty business, which already accounts for about 22% of total sales. This move reinforces analyst confidence in Sun Pharma's ability to maintain high single-digit revenue growth and counter generic price erosion in the US.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
The strategic exclusive license gives Sun Pharma immediate access to a rapidly growing US$3.7 billion ex-US and China market with a recently approved therapeutic (Lyrokaul in the EU). This expands its innovative specialty pipeline, which is a key driver of higher margins and long-term valuation.
Overweight: Pharmaceuticals, Specialty Healthcare
Trigger Factors:
- Launch timeline and commercial pricing of Lyrokaul in European markets.
- Regulatory progress and filings for Lerodalcibep in other licensed emerging markets and India.
- Quarterly revenue contribution from the Global Specialty portfolio.
Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
Industry Context
Historically, Indian pharmaceutical majors have relied heavily on the US generics market. However, severe pricing pressures and regulatory hurdles have forced players to diversify. Sun Pharma has successfully pioneered this shift among Indian peers. Its Global Specialty portfolio, featuring molecules like ILUMYA and ODOMZO, represents a major portion of its revenue mix. Entering the PCSK9 class places Sun Pharma in competition with established global biologics in the cardiovascular space, where patient adherence is traditionally high.
Key Risks to Watch
- Success relies on successful market entry and penetration across highly fragmented European and emerging markets.
- The PCSK9 class features powerful established biologics, which might limit market share expansion.
- Sun Pharma is responsible for regulatory filings and approvals in licensed jurisdictions where the drug is not yet approved.
Recent Developments
In July 2026, Sun Pharma reported its Q1 FY27 results, with net profit surging 27% YoY to ₹2,895 crore and consolidated revenue rising 10.5% YoY to ₹15,300 crore, led by strong performance in India formulations and the Global Specialty business. Separately, in April 2026, the company announced its largest-ever overseas transaction to acquire US-based Organon & Co in an all-cash deal with an enterprise value of US$11.75 billion, for which it completed a syndicated debt financing in August 2026.
Closing Insight
The Lerodalcibep licensing deal is a textbook execution of Sun Pharma's corporate strategy: acquiring late-stage, de-risked specialty assets to feed its global commercial engine. As the company prepares for the integration of its mega US$11.75 billion Organon acquisition, this targeted cardiovascular license adds high-margin organic depth without stretching the company's capital structures.

input.title: Sun Pharma Recalls Lidocaine Ointment, Nystatin Cream in US Over Quality Issues
input.content:
Sun Pharma Recalls Lidocaine Ointment, Nystatin Cream in US Over Quality Issues
New Delhi: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has initiated voluntary recalls of Lidocaine Ointment USP, 5%, and Nystatin Cream USP in the United States following quality-related issues identified during testing, according to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recall information.
The company is recalling 65,328 jars of Lidocaine Ointment USP, 5%, Spearmint Flavor, supplied in 50 g jars as a prescription-only product. The ointment is manufactured by Taro Pharmaceuticals Inc., Brampton, Ontario, Canada, and distributed in the US by Taro Pharmaceuticals U.S.A. Inc., Hawthorne, New York.
The affected product carries NDC 51672-3008-5 and belongs to Lot AD48154, with an expiration date of April 30, 2027.
The Lidocaine recall was initiated after the product failed to meet content uniformity specifications. According to the FDA recall information, the product was found to be out of specification for assay during analysis at the 24-month long-term stability station under storage conditions of 25°C and 60% relative humidity.
The recall is listed under D-0848-2026 and Event ID 99794 and has been classified as a Class II recall. The voluntary recall was initiated by the firm on August 31, 2026, while the FDA centre classification date was September 15, 2026. The recall covers nationwide distribution across the US.
A Class II recall refers to a situation in which use of, or exposure to, a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences, while the probability of serious adverse health consequences is considered remote.
Separately, Sun Pharma is recalling an undisclosed quantity of Nystatin Cream USP, a prescription-only antifungal product supplied in 15 g tubes, after the product failed to meet stability specifications.
The Nystatin Cream is manufactured by Taro Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., Haifa Bay, Israel, and distributed in the US by Taro Pharmaceuticals U.S.A. Inc., Hawthorne, New York. The product carries NDC 51672-1289-1.
The recall involves Lot AD49605 and Lot AD49606, both carrying an expiration date of May 31, 2027. The recall is identified as D-0872-2026 under Event ID 99876 and has an updated Class II classification.
The Nystatin recall was voluntarily initiated by the firm on September 14, 2026, while the FDA centre classification date was September 25, 2026. The distribution pattern covers the US nationwide.
The two recalls involve different Taro manufacturing facilities and separate recall numbers. The Lidocaine Ointment recall concerns an assay and content uniformity issue, while the Nystatin Cream recall relates to a failure of stability specifications. ETPharma also reported the recalls based on the FDA's latest enforcement report.
Lidocaine is a local anaesthetic used to temporarily numb an area and reduce pain by blocking pain signals from nerves, while Nystatin is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections. Both products are prescription-only drugs.

input.title: Nykaa partners with L’Oréal’s BOLD and completes 51% acquisition of Aminu Wellness
input.content:
The company popularly known as Nykaa, is an Indian consumer technology company operating across beauty, personal care, fashion and related categories. The company began as a digital-first beauty platform and has expanded into omnichannel retail, owned brands, fashion and B2B distribution.
The shares of Nykaa are currently trading atRs. 332.00, down by 0.91%. The company has a market capitalization of 95,094.59 crore. The stock’s 52 week high is Rs. 349.55 and its 52 week high is Rs. 227.90. In the past 6 months the stock has delivered a return of 36.05%.
What’s The News
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, also known as Nykaa, and BOLD, a corporate venture capital fund of L'Oreal, are partnering to nurture the future crop of Indian beauty and personal care brands.
The two organizations would be making investments into promising Indian startups in the beauty, personal care and wellness space, which have good consumer acceptance and unique product offerings, by taking minority equity stakes.
The partnership will combine Nykaa’s consumer ecosystem, omnichannel retail network and understanding of the Indian market with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, network and mentoring capabilities. The companies said the objective is to help promising Indian beauty businesses scale while allowing founders to continue running their brands independently.
Neither Nykaa nor L’Oréal has disclosed the names of the startups that will receive investment under the new collaboration or the timeline for the first investments.
Nykaa Completes 51% Acquisition of Aminu Wellness
Additionally, Nykaa has successfully completed the acquisition of 51% stakeholding in Aminu Wellness Private Limited on a fully diluted basis post the approval by the Board of Directors in the month of August 2026.
The acquisition has been completed on 24th September 2026, once all transaction documents have been signed and the shareholding has been allotted to the demat account of Nykaa. The acquisition has made Aminu Wellness a subsidiary of Nykaa.
The acquisition of 51% stake has been approved by Nykaa at an amount of Rs. 32 crores. Aminu Wellness is in the beauty and personal care product industry with a specialization in skincare products. The company was incorporated in June 2019. It has manufacturing expertise in cosmetic products.
Strategic Significance
Both the two initiatives add value to Nykaa as a beauty retailer since it is able to not only access emerging consumer brands but also scale the businesses through its retail and distribution network via the BOLD program.
The Aminu Wellness acquisition means that Nykaa is now in control of a majority-owned beauty and personal care business which specializes in skincare.
By June 30, 2026, Nykaa had reportedly provided services to over 60 million customers using its online platforms and run 324 offline beauty destinations. Some of the owned brands from the company include Nykaa Cosmetics, Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Collections and Earth Rhythm.
Financial Performance
Looking at the quarterly results of FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (Nykaa), the company’s consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29.10 percent YoY, from Rs. 2,154.94 crore in Q1 FY26 to Rs. 2,782.00 crore in Q1 FY27, and grew by 5.05 percent QoQ from Rs. 2,648.17 crore in Q4 FY26. The company’s consolidated total income stood at Rs. 2,791.31 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs. 2,164.27 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs. 2,657.32 crore in Q4 FY26.
In Q1 FY27, Nykaa’s consolidated net profit increased by 225.95 percent YoY, reaching Rs. 79.76 crore, compared with Rs. 24.47 crore in Q1 FY26. On a sequential basis, consolidated net profit increased by 1.28 percent from Rs. 78.75 crore in Q4 FY26. The profit attributable to equity shareholders of the parent stood at Rs. 80.01 crore, compared with Rs. 23.32 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs. 78.38 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company’s basic and diluted earnings per share stood at Rs. 0.28 in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs. 0.08 in Q1 FY26, registering an increase of 250 percent YoY. On a sequential basis, EPS increased from Rs. 0.27 in Q4 FY26 to Rs. 0.28 in Q1 FY27.
Investor Perspective
Collaboration with L'Oréal's BOLD unit and acquisition of Aminu Wellness can be seen as two different paths to extend Nykaa's beauty ecosystem. Whereas the partnership with BOLD will revolve around minority investments in emerging companies, the acquisition of Aminu Wellness means Nykaa owning a majority stake in an already established skincare-focused company.
In future, investors may keep a tab on the number of investments done through the BOLD-Nykaa partnership, performance and integration of Aminu Wellness, number of brands being developed internally by Nykaa and their contribution to its revenues.
Company Overview
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, better known as Nykaa, is an India-based consumer technology company that operates within the beauty and personal care, fashion, and other segments. It started out as a beauty platform that leverages technology but has since diversified to include omni-channel retailing, owned brands, and fashion and B2B distribution.
The company has also been diversifying its owned brands by leveraging its e-commerce platforms and physical store network to give access to beauty brands in the domestic and international markets. Nykaa has also extended its operations into the beauty segment in the Middle East region through its Nysaa platform.

input.title: Yahoo Finance
input.content:
French cosmetics giant L'Oréal and Indian retail company Nykaa have entered a partnership to jointly back emerging beauty and personal care brands in India.
Under the alliance, L'Oréal's corporate venture capital arm, Business Opportunities for L'Oréal Development (BOLD), will work alongside Nykaa to acquire minority stakes in Indian beauty and wellness companies that have "strong consumer traction and distinctive propositions".
The two companies clarified that the funding will be strictly financial and minority in scope, leaving founders with complete ownership and control over their operations, teams, culture and creative direction.
L'Oréal India managing director Jacques Lebel said: "Through BOLD and this partnership with Nykaa, we want to stand behind that talent—backing founders with capital, mentorship, and L'Oréal's beauty expertise, while leaving them free to build their brands their way."
Alongside funding, the backed brands will receive mentorship and guidance from BOLD and Nykaa, as well as access to L'Oréal's international expertise in beauty and Nykaa's omnichannel retail infrastructure and knowledge of consumer behaviour.
The companies said their goal is to "help ambitious Indian beauty founders scale faster and build enduring brands for India and the world".
BOLD was set up in 2018 and backs companies across the beauty value chain, focusing on two areas: beauty and wellness brands, and science and technology for beauty.
Nykaa was established in 2012 by Falguni Nayar and has since evolved from an online beauty retailer into a broader group covering beauty, fashion and B2B operations, with brands such as Nykaa Fashion, Nykaa Man and Nykaa Superstore under its umbrella.
Nykaa Beauty executive director and CEO Anchit Nayar said: "Combining our strong consumer ecosystem, deep retail network and wide distribution, along with L'Oréal's global beauty expertise will be an incredibly valuable asset to the next generation of founders as they look to build consumer brands that India can be proud of."
Earlier this week, the Competition Commission of India approved L'Oréal India's acquisition of Onesto Labs, the entity that operates the Innovist personal care platform.
"L'Oréal and Nykaa collaborate to fund Indian beauty brands" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.

Stocks to Watch Today, Friday, September 25, 2026: Nykaa, Waaree Energies, Dr Lal PathLabs, Sterlite Technologies, L&T Technology Services

Mumbai, Sept 25: Here are five stocks in focus on Friday, from a beauty-investment tie-up for Nykaa to a specialty-gases push for Waaree Energies to a diagnostics buyout for Dr Lal PathLabs to a data-center cabling expansion for Sterlite Technologies to an Industrial AI partnership for L&T Technology Services. Here’s what’s driving each stock and what to track through the session.
Nykaa (NYKAA): Inks investment deal with Loreal’s BOLD fund to invest in Indian beauty brands
Nykaa has inked an agreement with BOLD i.e. Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development to invest in the coming generation of high growth Indian beauty & personal care brands. As part of this pact, both companies will invest in a minority stake in brands that have high consumer pull at an early stage of growth or mid-stage growth. The investment would be financial in nature and founders of these brands can continue to lead the brands with their current team and vision. In addition to capital, Nykaa and BOLD will provide mentorship to their portfolio brands leveraging L’Oréal’s beauty experience and Nykaa’s panell distribution network. Anchit Nayar, CEO Nykaa Beauty commented that this is a natural extension of their decade long partnership with L’Oreal in India. While L’Oréal India MD Jacques Lebel said that India is one of the most dynamic beauty markets in the world. No details on cheque size and corpus amount were shared.
Waaree Energies (WAAREEENER): Subsidiary to enter specialty gases business
Waaree Energies’ wholly owned subsidiary Waaree Clean Energy Solutions has decided to enter into the Specialty Gases business in India. The company aims to be a one stop shop for Specialty Gases for all Semiconductor and Solar cell manufacturing companies in India. Specialty Gases like Silane, Ammonia and Nitrogen Trifluoride are some of the examples which are used during etching and cleaning and deposition processes while manufacturing chips and solar cells. India imports most of these specialty gases from few international players. This is yet another step by Waaree to move up in the Electronics and Solar Value Chain. Earlier last month the company inked an MoU with WPPL and SGL to manufacture semiconductors in Gujarat. Alongside the company is already manufacturing Solar Cells, Modules and Green Hydrogen. Company didn’t mention any capex outlay but this is a lucrative segment that is expected to see significant growth.
Dr Lal PathLabs (LALPATHLAB): Board approves acquisition of 70% equity shareholding in SN Genelab
Board of Directors of Dr Lal PathLabs has approved to acquire 70% of the shares held by the shareholders of SN Genelab at a cash consideration of upto Rs 168 Crore. SN Genelab will become a subsidiary of Dr Lal Pathlabs once the transaction is completed. This will further add to the list of acquisitions done by the company in the space of diagnostics and pathology. The transaction is expected to complete by 30th Nov 2026 subject to certain terms and conditions.
Sterlite Technologies (STLTECH): Upsizes its Neuralis Data Center Portfolio to include 6,912 Fibers
Sterlite Technologies has expanded its Neuralis Data Center portfolio to include Pre Terminated Fiber Trunk Assemblies ranging from 48F to 6912F. These trunks will help provide connectivity between the data center servers in High Density applications typically seen in AI and Hyperscale data centers. These are assembled and tested at the factory using MTP/MPO Connectors in both Singlemode and Multimode. This eliminates the time taken to terminate each individual fiber in the data center. This follows the company’s recent launch of US certified Plenum rated Fiber Trunk Assemblies. Sterlite has been riding on the back of its growing data center business and reported its highest open orders of over Rs 18,600 Cr along with a healthy growth in QoQ profits in its latest quarter. The company will now offer all fiber counts from 48 to 6912 in their portfolio.
L&T Technology Services (LTTS): Joins hands with Cognite for Industrial AI Solutions
L&T Technology Services has partnered with Cognite a global leader in Industrial AI to provide joint offerings of Industrial AI and Data solutions to asset intensive industries. This partnership will help augment LTTS’ Engineering Intelligence portfolio with Cognitive’s offering in Industrial AI. Cognite uses a combination of its Data Platform and knowledge graphs to understand and create context for complex assets. This is an extension of several other partnerships the company has made in the space of Engineering Intelligence over the past year. This will allow asset intensive clients to benefit from data generated from their operations and engineering to make informed decisions on assets.
Broader Read
We have Nykaa partnering with L’Oréal to invest in Indian beauty brands, Waaree entering the Specialty Gases business to supply chips and solar cells, Dr Lal Pathlabs acquiring a 70% stake in SN Genelab, Sterlite Technologies expanding its Data Center offering to higher fiber counts and L&T Tech Services partnering with Cognite for Industrial AI. There is a common thread among most of the stocks mentioned above. Whether it’s Nykaa trying to grow its reach in the beauty space or Waaree entering a new vertical to serve chip and solar cell manufacturing. And finally LTTS and STL are both trying to grow their footprint in Data Centers and Industrial AI. Let’s see how they fare in the markets today.

Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has partnered with BOLD, the corporate venture capital fund of L’Oréal, to jointly invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands.
The two companies will take minority stakes in high-growth beauty and wellness brands that have established consumer traction and differentiated offerings, according to a regulatory filing by Nykaa.
The investments will be financial and minority in nature, with founders retaining operational and creative control of their businesses. The brands will continue to operate independently with their existing teams, culture and creative direction.
Beyond providing capital, Nykaa and BOLD will offer mentorship and guidance to the companies they back. The partnership will bring together L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise and Nykaa’s omnichannel retail network and understanding of Indian consumers.
The companies said the aim was to help Indian beauty founders scale their businesses and build brands for domestic and international markets.
Nykaa and L’Oréal deepen partnership
Jacques Lebel, Managing Director of L’Oréal India, said India was “one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world”, pointing to changing consumer needs and the country’s growing community of entrepreneurs.
He said BOLD and Nykaa will support founders with capital, mentorship and L’Oréal’s beauty expertise while allowing them to retain control over how their businesses develop.
Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said: “Nykaa and L'Oreal have been partners in India for over a decade.”
Nayar said the experience gained from that relationship had helped Nykaa understand the challenges involved in building a promising brand into an enduring business.
He said Nykaa’s consumer ecosystem, retail network and distribution capabilities, combined with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, could support the next generation of Indian consumer brands.
What is BOLD?
BOLD, short for Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development, was launched in 2018 as L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund.
It makes minority investments in innovative, high-growth businesses across the beauty value chain. Its investments include beauty and wellness brands as well as companies working in science and technology for beauty.
Alongside funding, BOLD provides portfolio companies with access to L’Oréal’s beauty expertise, global network and mentoring while preserving their independence.
L’Oréal launched BOLD as part of its wider strategy of working with startups and emerging businesses. The French beauty group has a portfolio of 40 international brands and employs more than 95,000 people.
L’Oréal recorded sales of €44.05 billion in 2025, up 4% on a like-for-like basis and 1.3% on a reported basis.
Nykaa expands its beauty ecosystem
Nykaa began in 2012 as a digital-first beauty company and has since expanded into physical retail, fashion and B2B commerce.
Its businesses include Nykaa Fashion, Nykaa Man and Nykaa Superstore. The company has also entered the Middle East through Nysaa, its omnichannel beauty retail offering in the region.
Nykaa has built its own portfolio of consumer brands, including Nykaa Cosmetics, Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Collections, Nykaa Wanderlust, Nykaa Perfumes and Earth Rhythm. Its fashion labels include Nykd by Nykaa, KICA, 20 Dresses, RSVP and Gajra Gang.
As of 30 June 2026, Nykaa said it had served more than 60 million customers through its online platforms and had 324 offline beauty destinations.
The partnership with BOLD gives Nykaa and L’Oréal a joint investment route into emerging Indian beauty businesses while allowing the founders of the companies they back to continue running their brands independently.

input.title: Nykaa, L’Oréal’s BOLD to invest in Indian beauty startups
input.content:
Nykaa and L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital arm BOLD are joining hands to invest in Indian beauty, personal care and wellness startups, as established players look to gain exposure to the country’s growing pool of consumer brands.
BOLD is Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development, which was set up in 2018 as L’Oréal’s venture capital fund. It has invested in startups across the beauty value chain, particularly businesses focused on innovation and growth.
The latest partnership will see the two companies take minority stakes in high-growth businesses, with founders retaining ownership and operational control. Beyond capital, the partners will offer portfolio companies access to mentorship, industry expertise and their respective networks.
In February this year, Nykaa signed an exclusive pact with L’Oreal Luxe to manage end-to-end operations of skincare brand Kiehl’s in India. At a broader level, the two companies have worked for over a decade with each other, partnering to introduce and distribute several global beauty brands in India including L’Oreal’s Urban Decay, NYX Cosmetics, La Roche-Posay and Lancome onto Nykaa’s online and offline channels.
The size of the investments and the corpus committed to the latest initiative were not disclosed. The companies also did not name potential investee firms or specify when the first investments would be made.
The tie-up brings together Nykaa’s consumer and retail ecosystem in India with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise. For emerging brands, the combination could offer access to capital alongside distribution, consumer insights and industry capabilities as they seek to scale.
“India is one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world,” Jacques Lebel, managing director, L’Oréal India, said. Through BOLD and its partnership with Nykaa, L’Oréal aims to back entrepreneurs with capital, mentorship and beauty expertise while allowing founders to build their brands independently, he added.
BOLD combines financial investment with access to L’Oréal’s global network, beauty expertise and mentoring, while allowing founders to retain independence, Lebel said.
For Nykaa, the partnership comes as the company broadens its role in the beauty ecosystem beyond retail. It has built a portfolio of owned and in-house brands, including Nykaa Cosmetics, Dot & Key, Kay Beauty and Nykaa Collections, while also expanding into fashion and men’s grooming.
“Nykaa and L’Oréal have been large partners in India for over a decade,” Anchit Nayar, executive director and chief executive officer, Nykaa Beauty, said. The companies’ experience of working together has helped them understand what it takes to build a promising brand into an enduring one, he added.
Nayar said Nykaa’s consumer ecosystem, retail network and distribution capabilities, combined with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, could support emerging consumer brands.

input.title: Yahoo Finance
input.content:
MUMBAI, India and BRAMPTON, ON, Sept. 24, 2026 /CNW/ -- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Reuters: SUN.BO, Bloomberg: SUNP IN, NSE: SUNPHARMA, BSE: 524715, together with its subsidiaries and/or affiliated companies, "Sun Pharma") today announced the commercial availability of Taro-Methylphenidate ER for Canadian patients in Ontario and Quebec.
Taro-Methylphenidate ER is the first and only bioequivalent to Concerta® with an osmotic delivery system indicated for the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients six years of age and older.
"Finding the right treatment for someone with ADHD can be complicated," said Dr. Angelo Fallu, psychiatrist. "For the first time, we have not only a bioequivalent option but a molecule that uses the osmotic delivery system our patients have relied on for over 20 years to control their symptoms from morning to evening. This treatment option represents the only alternative with an osmotic delivery system available for our patients taking Concerta®."
ADHD is one of the most common neurodevelopmental disorders and is often diagnosed in childhood. ADHD presents as persistent inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that lead to significant functional impairments. It is estimated that 5.4% of Canadians have ADHD.i
"The osmotic delivery system in Taro-Methylphenidate ER maintains a stable and effective concentration of treatment throughout the day," said Dr. Martin Katzman, Psychiatrist and Clinic Director. "The osmotic delivery system acts to minimize the peaks, troughs, and variability sometimes seen in other formulations that can compromise real-world functioning and patient outcomes in ADHD."
"Taro-Methylphenidate ER is the only generic with data from two rigorous randomized crossover studies to demonstrate patient stability across normal days when switching from the brand name product," said Joel Lamoure, community and hospital pharmacist. "Maintaining restorative functionality in the patient can be achieved through consistent osmotic-based medication delivery systems. The patient's body cannot tell the difference between Taro-Methylphenidate ER and the branded product, and that is huge for ADHD patients and their stability."
"Sun Pharma is excited to launch this much-anticipated, osmotic delivery formulation of methylphenidate as a lower-cost alternative to Concerta® for the over 2 million Canadians affected by ADHD," said Raffaele Spadafora, Head of Specialty Generics.
Taro-Methylphenidate ER is currently reimbursed by Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) in Quebec and the Ontario Public Drug Program (OPDP).
"We continue to work with public and private formularies to support patient access in every province across the country" said Barb Pimentel, General Manager Generics and Consumer Healthcare, Sun Pharma.
About Taro-Methylphenidate ER Taro-Methylphenidate ER is indicated for the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in:
• children (6-12 years of age) • adolescents (13-18 years of age) • adults (>18 years of age)
- Should not be taken by children under 6 years of age - No data available in patients over 65 years of age - The effectiveness of Taro-Methylphenidate ER for more than 4 weeks in children and adolescents or 7 weeks in adults has not been systematically evaluated. If used for extended periods, physician should periodically re-evaluate.
Contraindications: Taro-Methylphenidate ER is contraindicated in: • Patients who are hypersensitive to methylphenidate or to any ingredients in the formulation or component of the container, thyrotoxicosis, advanced arteriosclerosis, symptomatic cardiovascular disease, moderate to severe hypertension, glaucoma, during treatment with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and also within a minimum of 14 days following discontinuation of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (hypertensive crises may result)
Most serious warning and precautions: • Drug dependence
Other relevant warnings and precautions: • General (oral use only), Fatigue, Information for patients, Carcinogenesis and Mutagenesis, hypertension and other cardiovascular conditions, pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebral vascular conditions, Sudden death and pre-existing structural cardiac abnormalities or other serious heart problems, Peripheral vasculopathy, including Raynaud's phenomenon, Drug dependence, Driving and operating machinery, Thyrotoxicosis, Long-term suppression of growth, Potential for gastrointestinal obstruction, monitoring and laboratory tests, cerebrovascular disorders, Motor and verbal tics, and worsening of Tourette's, Serotonin toxicity/serotonin syndrome, Increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma, Aggression, anxiety and agitation, Emergence of new psychotic or manic symptoms, Pre-existing psychosis, Screening patients for bipolar disorder, Suicidal behaviour and ideation, Priapism, Teratogenicity, Pregnancy women, Breast-feeding, Geriatrics, Pediatrics
For more information: • For important information on conditions of clinical use, contraindications, warnings, precautions, adverse reactions, drug interactions and dosing, please consult the product monograph at https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/index-eng.jsp. The product monograph is available by calling Sun Pharma Inc at 1-800-268-1975.
About Sun Pharma in Canada Sun Pharma combines the power of a global network with localized research and care to address the unmet needs of Canadian patients, and health care providers, consistent with the Company's vision of Reaching People. Touching Lives.
Sun Pharma offers a wide range of affordable medicines for the Canadian population in specialty and niche segments coupled with a presence in the top 15 Canadian generic products.
About Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (CIN - L24230GJ1993PLC019050) Sun Pharma is a leading global pharmaceutical company with a presence in Innovative Medicines, Generics and Consumer Healthcare products. It is the largest pharmaceutical company in India and is a leading generic company in the US as well as Global Emerging Markets. Sun's high growth Global Innovative Medicines portfolio spans innovative products in dermatology, ophthalmology, and oncodermatology and accounts for about 22% of company sales. The company's vertically integrated operations deliver high-quality medicines, trusted by physicians and consumers in over 100 countries. Its manufacturing facilities are spread across five continents. Sun Pharma is proud of its multi-cultural workforce drawn from over 50 nations.

input.title: Nykaa brings haircare brand Oribe to India
input.content:
Nykaa brings haircare brand Oribe to India
                                Multi-brand beauty and lifestyle giant Nykaa has brought global premium haircare brand Oribe to the Indian market with an exclusive, omni-channel retail arrangement.
 
A selection of Oribe’s products are now available on Nykaa’s e-commerce store, on its shopping app, and at select Nykaa stores across India, the business announced in a press release. Oribe debuts with five products from its best-selling ‘Gold Lust’ collection: its Gold Lust Repair & Restore Shampoo, Gold Lust Repair & Restore Conditioner, Gold Lust Transformative Masque, Gold Lust Nourishing Hair Oil, and Gold Lust Dry Heat Protection Spray.
 
Nykaa’s continued expansion of its global premium haircare offering reflects the country's trend towards consumers increasingly investing in high-performance, luxury haircare products. The segment is one of the fastest-growing segments within beauty, according to Nykaa.
“We’re excited to share the Oribe story and expand our footprint by launching with Nykaa in India,” said Oribe Hair Care’s vice president, commercial growth salon Asia Eddie Wan in a press release. “We look forward to enhancing the consumer experience across all touchpoints by providing a new destination for consumers to discover Oribe.”
 
Founded by hairstylist Oribe Canales alongside beauty industry veteran Daniel Kaner, Oribe follows a fragrance and design-led approach to beauty, according to the brand. Known for its signature ‘Côte d’Azur’ fragrance, Oribe was launched in 2008 and is headquartered in New York.

input.title: NSE pips Sun Pharma, Titan Company, Adani Enterprises, Infosys in terms of market cap
input.content:
The NSE stock has made its market debut only on BSE as per SEBI rules, which disallow shares of a stock exchange to be listed on its own platform.
NSE listing: Shares of National Stock Exchange of India Ltd (NSE) listed on BSE at Rs 1800 per share on Thursday, implying a premium of 0.84% to the IPO price. With this market debut, the stock has entered the league of top 10 Indian firms listed in terms of market cap on BSE. The IPO price of the issue was Rs 1,785 per share. It has become the 11th most valued firm in terms of market cap on BSE.
Post the mega IPO's market debut, market cap of India's largest exchange by volumes stood at Rs 4.53 lakh crore. It lags behind companies such as HUL (Rs 4.55 lakh crore), L&T (Rs 5.35 lakh crore) and Bajaj Finance (Rs 6.21 lakh crore) in terms of market capitalisation on BSE. The NSE stock has made its market debut only on BSE as per SEBI rules, which disallow shares of a stock exchange to be listed on its own platform.
On the other hand, NSE has crossed Sun Pharma (4.47 lakh crore), Titan Company (Rs 4.32 lakh crore), Adani Enterprises (Rs 4.21 lakh crore) and Infosys (Rs 4.16 lakh crore) in terms of market capitalisation on BSE.
NSE shares were offered in a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, with a minimum lot size of eight equity shares and subsequent applications in multiples of eight. The issue raised Rs 22,562 crore from investors and attracted more than 38.4 lakh applications, with bids worth over Rs 90,300 crore.
Advertisement
Among investor categories, qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the subscription demand, with their reserved portion being subscribed 12.68 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 6.55 times, while the retail portion saw a subscription of 1.39 times. The employee quota was subscribed 2.40 times.
The NSE IPO was managed by a consortium of 20 book-running lead managers, while MUFG Intime India is acting as the registrar to the issue.

input.title: Nykaa adds luxury haircare brand Oribe to India portfolio
input.content:
New Delhi: Nykaa has launched luxury haircare brand Oribe in India, adding the brand to its premium beauty portfolio.
Oribe, founded by hairstylist Oribe Canales and beauty industry executive Daniel Kaner, will initially enter the Indian market with five products from its Gold Lust collection.
The range includes the Gold Lust Repair & Restore Shampoo, Repair & Restore Conditioner, Transformative Masque, Nourishing Hair Oil and Dry Heat Protection Spray.
The brand’s India entry comes as premium and high-performance haircare products gain wider adoption among consumers looking for specialised formulations and salon-led beauty routines.
Commenting on the launch, Eddie Wan, Vice President, Commercial Growth Salon Asia for Oribe Hair Care, said, “We’re excited to share the Oribe story and expand our footprint by launching with Nykaa in India. We look forward to enhancing the consumer experience across all touchpoints by providing a new destination for consumers to discover Oribe.”
Oribe’s products combine haircare formulations with fragrance and design-led packaging. The brand’s Gold Lust range is positioned around repair, hydration, heat protection and frizz control.
The products are now available on Nykaa.com, the Nykaa app and at select Nykaa stores across India.

CHMP recommends marketing authorization for Cosentyx in polymyalgia rheumatica

The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) has adopted a positive opinion recommending marketing authorization for Novartis Cosentyx (secukinumab) in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). The recommendation positions the drug as the first interleukin-17A (IL-17A) inhibitor licensed in Europe for this condition, targeting adults with inadequate response to steroids or relapse during steroid taper.
Clinical Trial Data
The opinion follows results from the pivotal REPLENISH Phase III trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at the 2026 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Congress. The global, randomized, double-blind study evaluated efficacy and safety across 27 countries.
Key findings from the trial include:
Metric
Outcome
Primary Endpoint
Met for both 300mg and 150mg arms
Sustained Remission
Doubled vs placebo at week 52
Safety Profile
Consistent with established profile; no new signals
Steroid Exposure
Reduced cumulative dose via steroid-sparing effect
Patients were randomized into three arms: Cosentyx 300mg, Cosentyx 150mg, or placebo, all combined with a 24-week steroid taper regimen. Both active treatment arms met all primary and secondary endpoints, including complete sustained remission and time until additional treatment was needed through week 52.
What the Numbers Show
The data reveals a divergence between current standard-of-care limitations and the drug’s efficacy. While long-term steroid use—the existing standard—is associated with significant risks like osteoporosis and diabetes, Cosentyx delivered a steroid-sparing effect without introducing new safety signals. This suggests a potential shift in risk-benefit profiles for PMR patients, who currently face up to 40% relapse rates in the first year under conventional therapy.
Regulatory Pathway
Following the CHMP recommendation, the European Commission is expected to issue a final decision within approximately two months. If approved, Cosentyx will expand its portfolio beyond current indications in psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis, ankylosing spondylosis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, and hidradenitis suppurativa.
Patrick Horber, M.D., President of International at Novartis, stated that the approval would represent an important step in transforming care for those living with PMR, building on the drug’s established impact in autoimmune disease.

Sun Pharma Unveils Investor Presentation
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has shared its latest investor presentation, offering a comprehensive overview of its business operations, financial performance, and strategic initiatives. The presentation, dated September 22, 2026, outlines the company’s trajectory as a leading global specialty generic company and its commitment to creating lasting value.

input.title: Cyient (NSE:CYIENT): Why Did Independent Director Nitin Prasad Cease His Role?
input.content:
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT) filed an intimation on 22 September 2026 under Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, disclosing that Mr. Nitin Prasad (DIN: 05261866) ceased to be a Non-Executive Independent Director upon completion of his three-year term on 21 September 2026.
Key Highlights
- Mr. Nitin Prasad (DIN: 05261866) ceased as Non-Executive Independent Director of Cyient Limited effective 21 September 2026 at midnight upon completion of his three-year tenure.
- Alongside his board role, Mr. Prasad also ceased to be a member of the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the company with immediate effect.
- The cessation is attributed solely to completion of tenure and is not a resignation; the filing confirms no other material reasons are involved.
- The disclosure was made in compliance with Regulation 30 read with Schedule III, Part A, Para A (7B) of SEBI Listing Regulations and the SEBI Circular dated 13 July 2023.
About the Company
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), headquartered at Madhapur, Hyderabad, is a global engineering and technology solutions company. It serves clients across aerospace, defence, utilities, medical technology, semiconductor, and communications sectors. The company delivers design, engineering, manufacturing, and digital transformation services from delivery centres across India, Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific, with CIN L72200TG1991PLC013134.
Announcement in Detail
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, Cyient Limited informed both BSE (Scrip Code: 532175) and NSE (Scrip Code: CYIENT) that Mr. Nitin Prasad completed his three-year term as an Independent Director on 21 September 2026 at 24:00 hours IST. The filing, signed by Deputy Company Secretary Ravi Kumar Nukala, confirms the cessation was due exclusively to the expiry of his prescribed tenure period.
Simultaneously, Mr. Prasad ceased his membership of the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The Annexure A attached to the filing explicitly states that the cessation is not attributable to any other reason beyond tenure completion, and the item relating to confirmation of no other material reasons is noted as not applicable to a resignation scenario, since this is a scheduled end of term.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the departure is a scheduled governance event rather than a mid-term exit, which the filing distinguishes clearly from a resignation. The disclosed terms indicate that no additional material reasons, disputes, or covenant-related concerns have been cited by Mr. Prasad, reducing uncertainty around the circumstances of the change.
Shareholders will observe that the company's board composition has changed with the exit of one independent director and the concurrent loss of that member from the Leadership, Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The filing does not disclose a replacement appointment, so investors may wish to monitor future exchange filings for a successor nomination to assess whether the board retains the required independent director quorum under SEBI norms.
Sector / Market Context
SEBI's LODR framework requires listed companies to maintain a minimum proportion of independent directors on their boards, with stricter norms for companies with a non-executive chairperson. The engineering and technology services sector in India, which includes players like Cyient, has seen increasing regulatory focus on board-level governance disclosures following SEBI's enhanced Regulation 30 circular of July 2023, which mandated more structured and timely disclosure of director-level changes across all listed entities.
