input.title: Lenskart Gold Membership as a Customer Retention Innovation
input.content:
Lenskart Gold Membership as a Customer Retention Innovation
Industry & Competitive Context
India's eyewear industry was valued at approximately USD 9.2 billion in FY25, according to a RedSeer-authored market study cited in Lenskart's DRHP, and is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of roughly 13%, reaching about USD 17.2 billion (₹1,483 billion) by FY30. Within this market, prescription eyeglasses account for roughly 73% of value, with sunglasses and contact lenses making up smaller shares. Organised retail chains and branded omnichannel players as opposed to independent local opticians held only about 19–24% of the market as of FY24/FY25 on RedSeer's estimates, with the balance held by unorganised, single-outlet opticians and street vendors. This structural fact is central to the industry's competitive logic: the largest addressable growth pool is not share taken from branded rivals but conversion of unorganised, one-time, discretionary purchasers into a repeat-purchase, branded relationship.
Lenskart's own market-sizing has been publicly contested by its principal listed competitor. Titan Eye+ has stated the Indian organised eyewear opportunity is closer to USD 3.4 billion, against Lenskart's disclosed USD 9.2 billion estimate a dispute that surfaced in financial media coverage around Lenskart's IPO in late 2025, with Titan arguing that Lenskart's larger figure incorporates unorganised-sector and latent-demand estimates rather than organised retail sales alone. Beyond Titan Eye+, named competitors identified in Lenskart's own disclosures and in financial press coverage include Specsmakers, Vision Express, Warby Parker, and the Italian conglomerate EssilorLuxottica.
Lenskart, founded in 2010, is documented in its DRHP as India's largest seller of prescription eyeglasses by volume in FY25, operating an integrated omnichannel model online, mobile app, and physical retail with manufacturing centralised in Bhiwadi and Gurugram (India) and supported by facilities in Singapore and the UAE. As of March 31, 2025, the company operated 2,723 stores globally (2,067 in India, 656 overseas); by June 30, 2025 this had risen to 2,806 stores (2,137 in India), and the company subsequently announced plans to add roughly 450 stores in FY26, taking its global footprint past 3,150 outlets across 14 countries. In FY25, Lenskart reported revenue from operations of ₹6,652.5 crore, up 22.5% year-on-year from ₹5,427.7 crore in FY24, alongside its first full-year net profit of ₹297.34 crore (versus a net loss of ₹10.15 crore in FY24). The company listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025 following an IPO that was subscribed 28.26 times.
Brand Situation Prior to the Membership Program
Lenskart Gold was launched in 2018, at a stage when Lenskart was primarily known as a high-growth online-first eyewear retailer expanding into physical retail. The company's own press communication at launch, issued via its founder and CEO Peyush Bansal, framed the program as a mechanism to reward customers who purchase eyewear repeatedly, drawing an analogy to how consumers already own multiple wardrobe items for different occasions and could similarly own multiple pairs of eyewear. At launch, the membership was priced at ₹500 per year and offered a "Buy One, Get One" benefit across the company's John Jacobs and Vincent Chase private-label brands, redeemable from the customer's very first purchase and shareable with family members through a single registered mobile number.
Strategic Objective
Lenskart's own IPO disclosures frame Gold as one of several instruments alongside store network expansion, remote eye-testing infrastructure, and app-led engagement intended to convert episodic eyewear purchasers into a recurring, higher-frequency customer base. This is consistent with the category's underlying economics described above: with prescription eyeglasses typically replaced infrequently and much of the market unorganised and price-driven, a paid annual membership tied to a "second pair free" mechanic gives the company a structural reason for customers to make more than one purchase per membership cycle, and to consolidate multiple purchases (spectacles, sunglasses, contact lenses) within a single brand relationship rather than splitting them across the unorganised or organised competitive set.
The program's subsequent evolution Lenskart Gold Max launched in FY2024 and Lenskart Gold Max Pro launched in FY2025, according to Lenskart's official IPO investor-education note prepared by Axis Capital indicates a stated intent to tier the offer, extracting more value from higher-intent members through an escalating benefits ladder rather than a single flat membership.
Program Architecture & Execution
Lenskart operates its "Gold" membership in India and select international markets, distinct from a separate points-based loyalty scheme run through its Japanese/Southeast Asian subsidiary Owndays, which allows customers to earn redeemable points for purchases rather than a flat pre-purchased discount. According to the Axis Capital IPO note (drawing on the DRHP), Lenskart had 0.71 crore (7.1 million) Gold members in India as of June 30, 2025. A separate DRHP-based analysis published by financial-data platform Entrackr put India membership at 68 lakh (6.8 million) as of March 31, 2025 a figure broadly consistent with the Axis Capital number three months later. A further analytical write-up by Datum Intelligence, also drawing on DRHP disclosures, reported a considerably larger figure of 13.4 million members by H1 FY26, up from 3.4 million in FY23 a near four-fold increase over three years. Because these three sources do not specify identical geographic scope (India-only versus a possible broader/global count), this case reports all three as documented, rather than reconciling them into a single number; no single authoritative, unambiguous global membership figure is available from Lenskart's own primary filings as reviewed for this case.
On subscription revenue specifically, the Datum Intelligence analysis reports that Gold-related subscription income rose from ₹65.6 crore in FY23 to ₹108 crore in FY25, and reached ₹63.2 crore in the first half of FY26 alone already about 60% of the full FY25 total, which the source frames as a signal of renewal momentum. Separately, Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting shows a broader "services" revenue line which bundles membership income with home eye-checkup and training revenue growing 27% year-on-year to ₹133 crore in FY25, expressly attributed in the DRHP to the expansion of the Gold program. These are two different, only partially overlapping revenue lines (membership subscription alone versus a wider services bucket that includes membership), and both are reported here exactly as disclosed rather than merged.
On program mechanics, Lenskart's own loyalty page states that the Buy-One-Get-One benefit is valid on the company's Vincent Chase, Lenskart Air, John Jacobs, Hooper, and New Balance-branded eyewear (across eyeglasses and sunglasses combinations), is usable up to twice a month, is honoured across the app, website, 1,200-plus stores, and the company's home try-on service, and can be shared with family and friends by using the registered mobile number as the membership identifier. Consumer-facing deal-aggregator reporting (which carries lower editorial authority than a press release or the DRHP, and is flagged as such here) additionally describes a tiered structure in which the base Gold membership is priced around ₹500 per year, while Gold Max, priced higher, adds a 5% cashback on orders, free eye tests, and a 10% discount on Aqualens-branded contact lenses. These tier-specific prices are not confirmed in the DRHP excerpts reviewed for this case and should be treated as secondary-source reporting rather than official company disclosure.
On distribution, publicly available consumer-deal reporting describes Lenskart bundling free or discounted Gold/Gold Max memberships through partnerships with digital-payments and super-app platforms, including PhonePe, Google Pay, Times Prime, CRED, Swiggy One, and Zomato.
Positioning & Consumer Insight
The consumer insight articulated publicly by Lenskart at the program's 2018 launch via its CEO's own words in company press material was that eyewear was shifting from a single-purpose medical necessity to a category in which consumers might reasonably want multiple pairs for different occasions, in the way they already own multiple pairs of shoes or outfits. The Buy-One-Get-One structure operationalises that insight directly: rather than discounting a single pair, it monetises the second purchase decision, nudging a customer who came in for a functional prescription pair toward also acquiring a sunglasses pair or a second style, within the same brand.
The program's family-sharing mechanic allowing the same phone-number-linked membership to be used across a household extends the insight from an individual to a household unit, which is strategically significant in a market where eyewear purchases are often clustered by family occasion (school-age children, ageing parents needing corrective lenses, etc.). This mechanic is documented directly on Lenskart's own website and is not a third-party inference.
The tiering into Gold, Gold Max, and Gold Max Pro (FY2024 and FY2025 respectively, per the Axis Capital IPO note) suggests a positioning shift from a single flat-rate loyalty instrument toward a value-laddered subscription business, in which higher-paying members receive incremental benefits (cashback, additional category discounts). No verified public information is available on the relative mix of members across these three tiers, nor on differential purchase behaviour by tier.
Media & Channel Strategy
What is documented is
(a) the program's channel presence across Lenskart's own app, website, and 1,200-plus physical stores, as stated on the company's official loyalty page, and
(b) its bundling into third-party platform ecosystems (PhonePe, Google Pay, Times Prime, CRED, Swiggy One, Zomato) as reported in consumer deal-aggregator coverage, which functions as a distribution and acquisition channel rather than a media campaign in the traditional sense.
At the company level (not specific to Gold), Lenskart disclosed total marketing costs of ₹448 crore in FY25, up 27% year-on-year, according to DRHP-based reporting by Entrackr but this figure covers the company's overall marketing spend across brand and performance channels, and cannot be attributed specifically to the Gold membership program. No breakdown isolating loyalty-program marketing spend from the ₹448 crore total is available in public sources reviewed.
Business & Brand Outcomes
The following outcomes are documented in the sources cited and are reported here without extrapolation:
Membership scale reached 0.71 crore (7.1 million) in India as of June 30, 2025, per the Axis Capital IPO note; a separate DRHP-based estimate put it at 68 lakh (6.8 million) as of March 31, 2025 (Entrackr); and a third analytical source (Datum Intelligence) reported a figure of 13.4 million by H1 FY26 against 3.4 million in FY23, describing this as a near four-fold increase over three years. As noted above, these figures are not necessarily measuring an identical scope and are presented as separately sourced, rather than reconciled.
Subscription-linked revenue rose from ₹65.6 crore (FY23) to ₹108 crore (FY25) to ₹63.2 crore in H1 FY26 alone, per the Datum Intelligence DRHP-based analysis. The broader "services" revenue line that includes membership income, alongside home eye-checkup and training revenue, grew 27% to ₹133 crore in FY25, per Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting, which explicitly attributes this growth to Gold program expansion.
Lenskart's overall annual transacting customer base rose 23% to 99 lakh (9.9 million) in FY25, and unit eyewear sales rose 30% to 2 crore (20 million) pairs, per Entrackr's DRHP-based reporting company-wide figures that provide relevant context for the scale of the customer base into which the Gold program is embedded, though they are not membership-specific metrics.
Lenskart was named "India's Most Trusted Eyewear Brand of 2025" by TRA Research, according to the company's own IPO investor-education note a brand-level, third-party-adjudicated recognition disclosed by the company, though not directly attributable to the Gold program in the source material.
The company's IPO in which loyalty-driven recurring revenue was cited by DRHP-based commentary as a contributing narrative to its "sticky ecosystem" positioning was subscribed 28.26 times overall (40.35x in the Qualified Institutional Buyer category) when it closed on November 4, 2025, at a price band of ₹382–402 per share, according to Business Standard's reporting of exchange data. This is a company-level capital-markets outcome, not a Gold-specific outcome, and should be read as market validation of Lenskart's overall business model rather than direct evidence of the membership program's individual contribution.
Strategic Implications
Three implications follow directly from the documented facts above, without extending into unverified inference about mechanisms Lenskart has not disclosed.
First, Lenskart's membership architecture illustrates a route to building recurring revenue inside a category prescription eyewear that is structurally low-frequency at the level of a single product but can be made higher-frequency at the level of a household relationship, through mechanics (BOGO, family sharing, multi-tier upgrades) that are documented as central to Gold's design. The near four-fold membership growth reported by Datum Intelligence over three years, alongside the DRHP's own attribution of services-revenue growth to Gold's expansion, indicates the program has scaled meaningfully as the company approached its public listing, even though the precise financial contribution and profitability of the program are not independently disclosed.
Second, the tiering strategy Gold, then Gold Max (FY2024), then Gold Max Pro (FY2025) reflects a standard subscription-business pattern of introducing higher-value tiers once a base membership has proven adoption, a sequencing that is documented in the company's own IPO note rather than inferred. This suggests Lenskart's leadership treats the membership program as an evolving product line in its own right, not a static promotional device.
Third, the public dispute over market sizing between Lenskart and Titan Eye+ with the two companies citing materially different addressable-market figures ($9.2 billion versus $3.4 billion) is now a matter of public record following Lenskart's listing, and it illustrates a broader implication for any retailer that leans on unorganised-market conversion (rather than organised-competitor share capture) as its primary growth narrative to public-market investors: the credibility of that narrative, and by extension of loyalty-led conversion mechanisms like Gold, is now subject to ongoing public and analyst scrutiny in a way it was not while Lenskart was a private company.
Discussion Questions
- Lenskart discloses at least three different membership-count figures (7.1 million India-only as of June 2025; 6.8 million India-only as of March 2025; 13.4 million globally as of H1 FY26) drawn from different secondary interpretations of the same DRHP. As an analyst evaluating this business ahead of investment, how would you reconcile or interrogate these figures, and what does the discrepancy itself suggest about the reliability of loyalty-program metrics in IPO disclosures generally?
- Gold's core mechanic Buy One, Get One effectively monetises a second purchase decision rather than discounting the first. What are the margin and inventory implications of this design choice compared with a simple percentage-discount loyalty program, and under what category conditions (purchase frequency, unit economics, private-label mix) does a BOGO membership make more sense than a points-based scheme like Owndays'?
- Lenskart operates two structurally different loyalty models in parallel a flat-fee BOGO membership (Gold, in India and select markets) and a points-accrual scheme (Owndays, in Japan/Southeast Asia). What might explain this divergence by geography, and what should a multinational retailer consider before deciding whether to standardise a single loyalty architecture globally versus letting acquired subsidiaries retain their own models?
- The DRHP attributes 27% growth in "services revenue" (which bundles membership, eye-checkups, and training) to Gold's expansion, but does not disclose the standalone profitability of the membership program. Why might a company choose to disclose top-line growth attribution for a program while withholding its unit economics, and what should this signal to a public-market investor evaluating the durability of that growth?
- Titan Eye+ and Lenskart publicly disagree on the size of the addressable Indian eyewear market by a factor of nearly three. If Lenskart's loyalty-led strategy depends on converting unorganised-market, first-time buyers (as opposed to taking organised-market share from Titan), how should an investor's confidence in Gold's long-term contribution to revenue be affected by which of the two market-sizing narratives proves closer to reality?

input.title: From Nykaa to Traker: Pradeep Khandekar's Tech-Led Vision Drives Traker Past 1 Lakh+ App Downloads in India
input.content:
From Nykaa to Traker: Pradeep Khandekar's Tech-Led Vision Drives Traker Past 1 Lakh+ App Downloads in India
.
	Mumbai, India: From leading engineering at Nykaa to building a homegrown mobility and logistics platform, Pradeep Khandekar’s journey from Nykaa to Traker has reached another significant milestone. The application has crossed 1 lakh+ app downloads, strengthening its growing presence in India’s technology-driven transportation ecosystem.
	For users searching for a reliable cab service in Mumbai, cabs in Mumbai, bike taxi in Mumbai, auto rides or local transportation, the brand is building a multi-service experience designed to bring everyday transport options together. At the same time, its Boss Partner solution connects bike, auto, cab and mini truck partners with technology-enabled earning choices. It is now available in Mumbai, Pune, Indore and Hyderabad.
	The milestone therefore represents growth on both sides of the ecosystem—customers looking for convenient transportation and drivers looking for flexible work.
From Nykaa to Building a Mobility Business
	Before founding the venture, Pradeep Khandekar developed extensive experience in engineering and digital product development.
	He served as VP Engineering at Nykaa, working with engineering teams across mobile applications, product strategy and planning. He later served as CTO at RupeeBoss, leading technology across mobile, desktop, Android and iOS environments.
	Today, Khandekar is applying that technology-first experience to the venture, developing a digital service built around the everyday transportation needs of Indian customers and transport partners.
Making Everyday Travel Simpler for Users
	The business is positioning itself as more than a traditional cab booking app.
	Through one interface, users can access:
- Bike rides
- Auto rides
- Car rides
- Mini truck services
	For someone searching for online cab booking in Mumbai, a quick bike taxi, or an online solution for everyday local travel, the service aims to simplify the process by providing multiple vehicle categories within one ecosystem.
	Features such as digital booking, partner and vehicle information, live trip visibility and digital payment options are designed to give customers greater convenience throughout their journey.
	By combining passenger rides with goods transportation, the service can also support people whose needs extend beyond daily commuting—from booking a car to arranging a mini truck for local goods movement.
Building Opportunities for Driver Partners
	The other half of the brand’s growth story is its expanding partner community.
	The Traker Boss Driver Partner App supports two-wheeler riders, auto operators, cab drivers, mini truck operators and independent vehicle owners.
	For people searching for a bike driver app, cab driver app India, auto partner solution or driver partner service, the technology is designed to simplify ride management while offering flexible earning options.
	Partner-focused features include digital onboarding, real-time trip information, earnings visibility, weekly payouts and support.
	The brand has also introduced its Driver Loyalty Rewards Program, under which eligible partners who meet the required daily activity and trip criteria while maintaining zero cancellations can receive an additional ₹100 in their wallet.
	The initiative recognises transport partners who consistently contribute to a reliable customer experience.
One Technology Ecosystem for Customers and Drivers
	What differentiates the venture’s journey is the connection between both sides of urban transport.
	Customers need convenient and dependable rides. Drivers need access to trip opportunities and technology that helps them work efficiently. The service is being developed around both requirements rather than treating them separately.
	Two-wheelers. Auto. Cars. Mini Truck.
	By bringing these categories together, the venture is building a broader transport and logistics ecosystem for urban India.
	For Khandekar, the transition from Nykaa to this new venture represents the application of years of engineering and product experience to a new challenge: using technology to improve how people and goods move through Indian cities.
1 Lakh+ Downloads and the Journey Ahead
	Crossing 1 lakh+ app downloads is an important marker in the brand’s growth, but the team sees it as part of a larger journey.
	As the business strengthens its presence and expands its network, the focus remains on attracting more customers, creating earning options for driver partners and using technology to make local transportation easier to access.
	From a customer searching for cabs in Mumbai to a transport partner looking for flexible earning choices, the service is working to bring both sides of the ecosystem onto one connected network.
	The 1 lakh+ milestone signals growing momentum for that vision and a new chapter in Pradeep Khandekar’s journey from building technology at Nykaa to developing Traker for India’s evolving mobility market.
About Traker
	Traker Networks Private Limited is a technology-driven mobility and logistics business offering two-wheeler, auto, cab and mini truck services through its digital ecosystem. The brand connects customers seeking convenient transportation with partners looking for flexible earning options.

input.title: Cyient (NSE:CYIENT): Did CCI Clear Its Acquisition of Tao Digital Solutions Inc?
input.content:
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), in an exchange filing dated 26 August 2026, disclosed that the Competition Commission of India approved its proposed acquisition of 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc., a US-incorporated company, under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002.
Key Highlights
- The CCI communicated its approval via a letter dated 25 August 2026, referencing combination registration number C-2026/06/1433 filed by Cyient on 15 June 2026.
- Cyient had originally disclosed a definitive agreement to acquire 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc. through an exchange filing on 30 May 2026.
- The CCI approved the combination under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002, following its meeting held on 25 August 2026.
- The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions; the CCI order confirming the approval is expected to follow the letter of communication.
About the Company
Cyient Limited (NSE:CYIENT), headquartered at Madhapur, Hyderabad, is a global engineering and technology solutions provider. The company delivers design, manufacturing, and digital technology services across aerospace, defence, medical devices, semiconductor, and rail industries, serving clients across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. It is listed on BSE (scrip code 532175) and NSE.
Announcement in Detail
In its filing under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Cyient confirmed receipt of the CCI's approval letter dated 25 August 2026. The commission considered the proposed combination in its meeting on the same date and cleared it under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002. The CCI's formal order is stated to follow the communication.
The combination notice bearing registration number C-2026/06/1433 was originally filed by Cyient with the CCI on 15 June 2026, under sub-section (2) of Section 6 of the Competition Act, 2002. The underlying definitive agreement to acquire the entire 100% stake in Tao Digital Solutions Inc., a company incorporated in the United States, was entered into by Cyient and disclosed to exchanges on 30 May 2026.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the CCI approval represents a material regulatory milestone in the acquisition process. The filing indicates the transaction has cleared a mandatory competition-law review. However, the disclosure specifies that customary closing conditions must still be satisfied before the deal concludes, meaning the acquisition is not yet complete at the time of this filing.
Shareholders will observe that the consideration structure and financial terms of the acquisition were not re-stated in this specific filing; those details, as disclosed on 30 May 2026, remain the applicable reference. The disclosed terms indicate any final impact on Cyient's consolidated financials will depend on the completion of remaining closing formalities.
Sector / Market Context
India's engineering research and development services sector has seen sustained cross-border acquisition activity as domestic players seek to expand digital and software-embedded engineering capabilities in North American markets. According to NASSCOM data, India's technology and engineering services exports have grown consistently, with engineering R&D services forming an expanding share of total IT-sector revenue, making inorganic international expansion a widely adopted strategic approach among listed Indian engineering services companies.

input.title: Cyient shares surge 8%: Targets by MOFSL, Antique, Choice, Nuvama post Investor Day
input.content:
Cyient Ltd shares rallied 8 per cent in Wednesday’s trade after a couple of brokerages raised their target prices on the stock following the midcap IT firm’s Investor Day. At the event, the management indicated a significant expansion in Cyient’s addressable market, from $100 billion in traditional ER&D outsourcing to $2.4-3.2 trillion by covering the full engineering lifecycle across nine value-chain stages.
This provided a much larger runway for future growth, Nuvama Institutional Equities said as it upped its target on the stock to Rs 1,050 from Rs 900.  On Wednesday, Cyient share price jumped 7.66 per cent to hit a high of Rs 1,054.60.
Cyient's DET (Digital, Engineering, and Technology) EBIT margin target is set at 15 per cent by FY28 against at 13.2 per cent in Q1. Cyient Semiconductors targets 4 times revenue growth by FY31 with 40 per cent gross margin and 20 per cent-plus EBIT, supported by Kinetic Technologies and increasing traction in its ASSP and ASIC businesses.
"We continue to value the stock using SotP methodology —DET business at 11 times FY28E PE and DLM at current market cap (post 20 per cent holdco discount). We now include semicon business (1x FY28E EV/sales) in our valuation," Nuvama said.
Inexpensive valuations limit downside potential, it said.
Choice Institutional, which attended Cyient's Investor Day, said the Investor Day takeaways strengthened the medium-term growth and earnings-quality thesis, although large-deal conversion and the pace of growth recovery remain key execution watchpoints. It maintained ‘Buy’ rating on Cyient and raise its target to Rs 1,200.

input.title: Top Gainers & Losers on 25 Aug: FACT, Vodafone Idea, Cyient, Paytm, Angel One, Pine Labs among top gainers
input.content:
The Indian stock market was lifted into positive territory by late-hour buying during Tuesday's trade, August 25, though the underlying sentiment remained fragile amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. After opening the session lower, the markets remained under pressure for most of the day before recovering in the final hour of trade. The Nifty 50 eventually settled 0.17% higher at 24,260, while the Sensex also ended the session in the green at 77,511, up 0.21% from its previous close. The broader market, however, delivered a mixed performance, with the Nifty Midcap 100 closing in the green while the Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 0.22%. Sectoral trends were also mixed, with pharma and consumer durables gaining nearly 1%. On the other hand, private banks and metal stocks emerged as the top losers. Meanwhile, in the commodity market, oil prices retreated after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced fresh sanctions against Iran and warned that countries continuing to do business with the Islamic Republic could face retaliation. President Donald Trump's pledge last week to unleash an “economic D-Day” against Tehran ultimately translated into fresh warnings aimed at cutting Iran off from the rest of the global economy. Asked why the US was not immediately imposing secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners, Bessent told reporters that he wanted countries to have an opportunity to shift away from Iran before it was too late, AP reported. The latest measures further escalated geopolitical tensions, with Iran warning that the new US sanctions announced on Monday would not bring peace to the region. Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Tehran would respond harshly to the expanded sanctions, including measures targeting countries that Iran believes are cooperating with Washington, as per the AP report. Fertilisers and Chemicals Travancore (FACT) emerged as the top performer, with the stock jumping 11.4% to ₹874 after Russia on Monday assured India of an uninterrupted supply of energy and fertilisers. The positive sentiment also lifted other fertiliser stocks, with Paradeep Phosphates surging 7% to ₹159. Beyond fertiliser stocks, Vodafone Idea shares settled 8% higher at ₹15.20 apiece amid reports of progress in its funding discussions with SBI. Cyient also posted a similar gain of 7%, settling at ₹975. Among new-age technology stocks, Paytm, Pine Labs and Groww gained 5.8%, 4.2% and 3.4%, respectively. Adani Enterprises and AWL Agri Business emerged as the top performers among Adani Group stocks, rising 3.7% and 3.5%, respectively. Capital market-linked stocks such as Angel One and HDFC AMC also settled higher, gaining 5.2% and 3.1%, respectively. Other stocks, including Laurus Labs, eClerx Services, Indus Towers, Chalet Hotels, Dixon Technologies and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, also surged more than 3%. Hindustan Copper shares emerged as the top loser, falling 7.2% after the government announced an offer for sale (OFS) at a floor price that was around a 10% discount to Monday's closing price. IIFL Finance and Data Patterns (India) also closed lower, declining 4.3% and 4.1%, respectively. Selling pressure in Balrampur Chini Mills extended further, with the stock falling another 3.9% to ₹668. Redington shares also declined 3.4% to ₹352, extending their weakness. Netweb Technologies, Ola Electric Mobility, Federal Bank, LT Foods, Elecon Engineering, Siemens Energy India, Sonata Software, Birlasoft, and Welspun Corp. were among the other major losers, with each falling more than 2.5%. input.title: SoftBank cuts Lenskart stakes for second time, sells  ₹2,888 cr worth shares to Goldman Sachs, Societe Generale, others
input.content:
SoftBank continues to offload its holding in Lenskart, selling shares worth ₹2,888 crore just two months after selling ₹2,873 crore worth of its stake in the eyewear retailer.
In the latest transaction, Japan-based SoftBank Group, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, offloaded a total of 4.5 crore equity shares in 22 tranches, amounting to a 2.58 per cent stake in Gurugram-based Lenskart, said the block deal data on the BSE.
In June, SoftBank sold a 3.25 per cent stake in Lenskart for ₹2,873 crore. Following the sale, shares of Lenskart Solutions fell 0.28 per cent to close at ₹659.70 apiece on the BSE on Monday.
The block deal saw participation from a wide range of institutional investors.
Domestic buyers included National Pension System Trust and mutual funds managed by SBI, Edelweiss, Nippon India, Franklin Templeton, HDFC, HSBC, ICICI Prudential, Motilal Oswal and Sundaram.
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance was also among the buyers.
Among foreign investors, financial services company Societe Generale picked up the largest number of shares, acquiring 1,07,35,000 shares, representing a 0.62 per cent stake.
This was followed by Goldman Sachs, which bought 84.31 lakh equity shares in Lenskart for ₹541.06 crore. Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund acquired 47.71 lakh shares for ₹306.17 crore, while Pennsylvania-based Vanguard Group Inc. picked up 37.28 lakh shares for ₹239.2 crore.
Other foreign investors that lapped up Lenskart shares included Ghisallo Capital Management, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Wasatch Global Investors, and Integrated Core Strategies Asia.
Other buyers included Frankfurt-based Universal Investment, Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois, Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System and Kuwait Investment Authority.
The shares were sold at an average price of ₹641.75 apiece, taking the combined deal size to ₹2,887.87 crore, the block deal data showed
As per the shareholding pattern for June 2026, SoftBank held a 9.86% stake in Lenskart, which appears to have reduced to 7.28% following the above-mentioned block deals. Meanwhile, HSBC MF held a 1.15% stake, while SBI Mutual Fund held a 2.44% stake in the company.
The latest transaction brought SoftBank's holding in Lenskart down to 7.28% from 9.86%, although it remains the second-largest public shareholder in the eyewear firm.
Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an arm of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, continues to be the largest public shareholder of Lenskart with a 9.77 per cent stake.
(With inputs from agencies)

input.title: From IPO mockery to Rs 1 lakh crore m-cap: Why investors are still betting on Lenskart’s vision
input.content:
Listen to this article in summarized format
The numbers made the valuation look even harder to digest. Even if Lenskart tripled its profits from that level over the next few years, the valuation would still work out to around 70x.
Retail investors did not hold back. The Rs 70,000-crore valuation quickly became fodder for social media. One X user calculated that with around 2,600 stores in India, each store was effectively being valued at around Rs 27 crore. The punchline: “Are they selling spectacles or diamond lenses?”
Another found the irony impossible to miss: “If Peyush Bansal pitched Lenskart’s valuation to Shark Tank’s Peyush Bansal, then he would have got rejected.”
Another drew comparisons with a familiar list of expensive IPOs: “To all the people who missed the lessons from Mamaearth, Paytm & Nykaa, don’t worry, here’s your latest chance.”
And yet, the market delivered an answer of its own
Fast-forward to 2026. Lenskart shares are up 50% so far this year. The company now commands a market capitalisation of Rs 1.15 lakh crore. The same stock that was mocked for being too expensive has continued to attract investors.
The reason, according to analysts, is increasingly less about the IPO valuation and more about what Lenskart is becoming.
Domestic brokerage Elara Capital believes Lenskart has built one of India’s most differentiated retail models by creating a full-stack eyewear ecosystem spanning the entire value chain. The brokerage draws a parallel with Titan Company Limited’s jewellery business, arguing that Lenskart could steadily compound market share gains and emerge as the category-defining leader in eyewear, much as Tanishq did in jewellery.
And Lenskart’s own numbers suggest that the company is not simply trying to sell more spectacles. It is building an eyewear business that spans everything from a Rs 500 pair of glasses to Rs 30,000 progressive lenses.
In its shareholders’ letter, the company said it had reached its largest-ever number of customers in “Real Bharat” with Rs 500 glasses, including lenses and warranty, sold profitably through Hustlr Club. At the other end of the spectrum, glasses with high-end Rodenstock and Tokai lenses, including progressive lenses priced at Rs 30,000, generated around Rs 250 crore in annual sales.
Then there is Owndays. Lenskart said glasses with premium Owndays lenses generated more than Rs 1,500 crore in annual sales, despite the business not having a presence in India two years ago.
The international story is also beginning to look different. Lenskart said its international business grew 38%, with an EBITDA margin before Ind AS 116 crossing 10%. The company believes the question is no longer whether the international business can work, but how far it can scale.
With Owndays, Lenskart now has one of Asia’s most respected brands. Meller, meanwhile, was a $35 million brand and is on track to become a $70 million brand.
What’s working for Lenskart?
1) Strong business model
At the heart of the Lenskart thesis is a model designed to reinforce itself as it grows. Elara points to revenue productivity of nearly Rs 25,000-30,000 per square foot, high gross margins driven by the company’s private-label-led model and an industry-leading store payback period of around 10-12 months.
But perhaps more important is whether Lenskart can keep bringing customers through the door. It can. The company is reporting same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 20%, which Elara sees as a key differentiator. Revenues across Tier I and Tier II markets are also nearly equal, suggesting that Lenskart’s growth is not dependent solely on India’s largest cities.
2) Full-stack retail infrastructure
According to Elara, Lenskart's advantage extends beyond its stores. The company has built a customer acquisition funnel around free eye testing while continuing to invest in technology to improve the customer experience. Its technology-enabled remote testing capabilities allow it to conduct nearly 600 eye tests per store every month.
The ambition is significantly larger. Lenskart is targeting 100 million eye tests over time, compared to the 23.7 million eye tests conducted in FY26.
Its backward integration has also moved beyond simply cutting costs. Elara Capital sees it as a strategic competitive advantage that gives Lenskart greater control over products, faster inventory turnover and next-day delivery across 78 cities.
That combination matters because it links the company’s stores, manufacturing and technology into one system, strengthening both customer experience and margin resilience.
That combination matters because it links the company's stores, manufacturing and technology into one system, strengthening both customer experience and margin resilience.
Buy, sell or hold Lenskart shares?
Jefferies has maintained its Buy rating on Lenskart and raised its target price to Rs 680. The brokerage said Q1FY27 further strengthens the company’s growth and margin expansion story. Market creation remains a key priority, with supply rather than demand emerging as a constraint in India, reflected in around 70,000 daily eye tests.
Lenskart has also strengthened its presence at the lower end with a fully loaded Rs 500 product, while premiumisation is emerging as another growth driver. Jefferies believes improving margins in the international business should address a key investor concern and sees potential for Meller to become the “Ray-Ban of the future.”
Morgan Stanley has an Overweight rating and a target price of Rs 666. The brokerage said Lenskart delivered another quarter of strong performance in Q1, with the beat driven largely by the international business. Strong performance, optimistic management commentary, and higher earnings estimates support its expectation of continued stock outperformance.
Goldman Sachs has an Accumulate rating and raised its target price to Rs 715. The brokerage said the growth and margin flywheel continues to deliver, pointing to significant margin expansion in the international business while SSSG remains elevated.
In India, Goldman Sachs sees volume-led revenue growth and operating leverage-driven margin expansion. It also identifies premiumisation as a new growth vector for the company.
Macquarie has an Outperform rating and raised its target price to Rs 675. The brokerage said India’s Q1 performance was in line with expectations, while the international business beat estimates on stronger margin expansion.
Macquarie remains positive on strong volume growth, continued premiumisation across lenses and frames, the attractive Rs 500 entry-level offering, and the potential for more than 10,000 stores in India. Stronger international margins have led to a 4% upgrade to its EPS estimates and an 8% increase in the target price.
For Lenskart, the market’s biggest shift may not be in its valuation, but in what investors are willing to believe about its future. The company has moved beyond being just an organised eyewear retailer, with a model that now spans value eyewear, premiumisation, eye testing, backward integration, and an expanding international business.

input.title: Nykaa posts ₹752 crore EBITDA in FY26, targets 4-5x growth by FY30
input.content:
Nykaa posts ₹752 crore EBITDA in FY26, targets 4-5x growth by FY30
- Revenue crossed ₹10,000 crore in FY26, growing 26% YoY
- EBITDA surged 59% to ₹752 crore, expanding margins to 7.5%
- Company targets 4-5x EBITDA growth and 90% same-day delivery by FY30
- Fashion segment achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY26
- ROCE doubled to 21.2% as net debt fell 47%
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Nykaa delivered strong financial performance in FY26, with revenue crossing the ₹10,000 crore mark and EBITDA growing 59% to ₹752 crore. The company reaffirmed its aggressive operational targets for FY30, aiming to scale GMV by 2.5-3 times and expand EBITDA by 4-5 times.
FY26 Financial Performance
The beauty and lifestyle retailer demonstrated significant operating leverage in FY26. Revenue grew 26% to over ₹10,000 crore, while EBITDA expanded disproportionately to ₹752 crore, pushing margins from 6% to 7.5%. This efficiency drove net profit (PAT) nearly triple to ₹204 crore, with PAT margin doubling to 2%.
Capital efficiency also improved markedly. Fixed asset turnover rose to 9.9 times, supported by asset-light businesses like Fashion and House of Nykaa. Working capital days reduced from 34 to 28 days due to tighter inventory and receivables management. Consequently, ROCE doubled from 11.3% to 21.2%, aided by a 47% reduction in net debt.
Strategic Targets for FY30
Nykaa projects substantial scale-up in both gross merchandise value (GMV) and profitability over the next four years. The company aims to deliver 90% of its orders on the same or following day across 19,000 pin codes by the end of FY30.
Segment Highlights
Beauty: The core vertical saw NSV grow 4x to over ₹8,500 crore, with GMV reaching approximately ₹15,000 crore. The omnichannel network expanded to 313 stores across 99 cities. Nykaa Now, the rapid delivery service, is available in 13 cities and will expand to over 25 by year-end.
Fashion: Nykaa Fashion achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY26, a significant milestone after scaling NSV 6x to nearly ₹1,450 crore. EBITDA margins improved from negative 11.3% to negative 2.6% over five years. The platform now serves 11 million customers.
House of Nykaa: The private label portfolio scaled 8x in GMV to approximately ₹3,200 crore. New launches contributed around 25% of FY26 GMV for key brands like Nykaa Cosmetics and Kay Beauty.
Superstore: The eB2B platform grew nearly 4x in three years to ₹1,200 crore GMV. EBITDA margins improved by 3,500 basis points over the same period, serving nearly 5 lakh retailers.
What the Numbers Show
The disparity between the projected GMV growth (2.5-3x) and EBITDA expansion (4-5x) suggests a strategic focus on operating leverage. By accelerating delivery timelines and optimizing working capital—evidenced by the reduction in working capital days from 34 to 28—Nykaa intends to drive efficiency that outpaces top-line volume growth. The doubling of ROCE to 21.2% alongside a 47% drop in net debt indicates that recent profitability gains are not just operational but also structural, driven by better capital deployment.

input.title: Cyient unveils ‘Nothing Less’ brand positioning
input.content:
Hyderabad: Cyient has unveiled its new brand positioning and promise, ‘Nothing Less,’ as the company strengthens its identity as a Global Lifecycle Engineering Services leader.
The positioning will anchor Cyient’s go-to-market strategy, reflecting its focus on creating value across the complete lifecycle of products and business-critical assets—from design and manufacturing to services. The company aims to build partnerships that deliver value over decades rather than being confined to individual projects.
The refreshed proposition brings together engineering expertise, domain knowledge, human intelligence and contextual AI to help customers navigate increasingly complex, intelligence-driven environments and improve performance, reliability and growth.
Cyient has defined the proposition through two complementary pillars: Intelligent Engineering and Embracing Intelligence. While Intelligent Engineering describes the company’s approach of combining engineering, digital and industry expertise, Embracing Intelligence focuses on bringing together people, data and AI to enable better decisions and outcomes.
Sukamal Banerjee, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Cyient Ltd, said the new positioning reflects the company’s evolution and future direction.
“Nothing Less is a reflection of how Cyient has evolved and where we are headed. As a Global Lifecycle Engineering Services company, we are expanding the value we deliver across the entire life of an asset, from design to manufacture to services.”
Banerjee added that competitive advantage is increasingly being shaped by the convergence of engineering expertise, human ingenuity and AI-driven intelligence. “We help customers solve complex challenges faster, improve outcomes, and unlock greater value throughout the lifecycle.”
The new positioning builds on Cyient’s engineering heritage dating back to its founding in 1991. Krishna Bodanapu, Executive Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Cyient, said the company has developed deep domain expertise while working with leading global organisations across demanding and mission-critical environments.
“This legacy of engineering excellence, customer focus, and value-driven ownership has shaped who we are today and sets the foundation for our next phase of growth,” Bodanapu said.
The brand refresh is also anchored in Cyient’s Values FIRST framework—Fairness, Integrity, Respect, Sincerity and Transparency—which the company said will continue to guide its relationships with customers and its way of working.
Through ‘Nothing Less’, Cyient is positioning its next phase around a broader engineering proposition that combines technology, human expertise and lifecycle engagement to deliver stronger outcomes for customers.

input.title: Cyient Unveils 'Nothing Less' Brand and Outlines Strategic Growth Targets at Investor Day
input.content:
Cyient Unveils 'Nothing Less' Brand and Outlines Strategic Growth Targets at Investor Day
Cyient has rebranded to 'Nothing Less' to cement its leadership in global lifecycle engineering services. Alongside this, the company's semiconductor arm has set strategic targets to quadruple revenue by FY31 (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified), backed by robust cash flows, a newly completed ₹720 crore buyback, and a $500 million post-money valuation for its chip division.
Market snapshot: Cyient has launched its new global brand positioning, 'Nothing Less,' marking its transition into an elite lifecycle engineering services provider. Additionally, the company has outlined ambitious growth targets for its semiconductor business to power four-times revenue growth by FY31 (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified) from its current combined base of $65.7 million. This strategic push follows a strong start to FY27, supported by stable engineering numbers, a completed capital return, and a high-valuation funding round for its semiconductor subsidiary.
Data Snapshot
- Cyient DET segment revenue reached ₹1,540 crore in Q1 FY27, representing a 10.6% year-on-year growth.
- The company successfully completed a ₹720 crore share buyback program, extinguishing 6.4 million shares at ₹1,125 per share.
- Cyient Semiconductors secured $10 million in strategic equity financing from Edelweiss at a post-money valuation of $500 million.
What's Changed
- Rebranding: Transitioned from traditional engineering services to a focused lifecycle engineering services model under the 'Nothing Less' positioning.
- Revenue Base Scale-Up: Cyient DET segment revenue increased to ₹1,540 crore in Q1 FY27, up 10.6% YoY from the corresponding period.
- Funding Injections: The newly carved-out Cyient Semiconductors completed a major $10 million financing round at a $500 million valuation, a substantial scale-up from its early setup phase.
Key Takeaways
- Strategic Rebranding: The 'Nothing Less' positioning represents Cyient's transition toward high-value, end-to-end lifecycle engineering consulting, aimed at capturing larger global R&D budgets.
- Semiconductor Momentum: Cyient Semiconductors is positioning itself as a custom power chip leader following its majority stake acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and a $500 million valuation round.
- Strong Capital Allocation: The completion of a ₹720 crore buyback at ₹1,125 per share signals robust cash reserves and proactive management efforts to return value to shareholders.
- M&A Integration: The pending closure of the TAO Digital Solutions acquisition by August 2026 is expected to add $40 million to $50 million in annual revenue, bolstering digital engineering capabilities.
SAHI Perspective
Cyient is executing a deliberate transition away from low-complexity IT outsourcing toward high-margin, asset-heavy lifecycle consulting in industries like aerospace and mobility. This shift shields the company from the commoditization currently impacting pure-play IT firms. By carving out its semiconductor business and securing high-profile acquisitions like Kinetic Technologies, Cyient is successfully building proprietary IP. While near-term discretionary R&D spending among global clients remains cautious, Cyient’s strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation provide the stability required to capture the next secular growth wave.
Market Implications
The successful integration of premium brand positioning and chip-level engineering could elevate Cyient’s billing rates and customer stickiness, distinguishing it from mid-size IT peers. The semiconductor and electronics design focus positions it as a direct beneficiary of India's domestic chip-manufacturing push, potentially unlocking long-term valuation rerating as IP-led revenues scale up.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
Cyient's sequential profit recovery, ₹720 crore capital return, and high-value semiconductor funding demonstrate robust financial health. Solid segment growth in DET and the imminent closure of the TAO Digital deal underpin a strong near-to-medium term outlook.
Overweight: Engineering Services, Semiconductors, IT Services
Trigger Factors:
- Imminent closure of the TAO Digital Solutions acquisition by the end of August 2026.
- EBIT margin expansion towards the company's mid-term target of 15%.
- Successful product revenue ramp-up in the high-power ASSP segment.
Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
Industry Context
Global engineering R&D spending is increasingly shifting toward digital engineering, connected products, and localized supply chains. In India, policy initiatives like the India Semiconductor Mission are acting as major catalysts for domestic chip design firms. Service providers that offer complete lifecycle management—from design to predictive maintenance—are best equipped to capture the majority of global R&D budgets.
Key Risks to Watch
- Execution risks regarding the integration of Kinetic Technologies and TAO Digital Solutions.
- Global client caution on discretionary R&D spend, particularly in the European rail transport sector.
- High competition from larger global engineering majors limiting the success of premium brand positioning.
Recent Developments
In July 2026, Cyient completed its ₹720 crore share buyback program, extinguishing 6.4 million equity shares. For Q1 FY27, Cyient DET reported a revenue of ₹1,540 crore and a normalized EBIT margin of 13.2%. Furthermore, Cyient Semiconductors closed a $10 million equity financing round with Edelweiss in May 2026.
Closing Insight
Cyient's evolution into an IP-rich lifecycle engineering partner is backed by strong execution and clean balance sheet indicators. Investors should watch the integration of its semiconductor acquisitions as the primary driver of its next growth cycle.

input.title: SoftBank pares nearly 2.6% stake in Lenskart for Rs 2,888 Cr
input.content:
SoftBank pares nearly 2.6% stake in Lenskart for Rs 2,888 Cr
In the latest transaction, SoftBank Group, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, offloaded 4.5 crore equity shares in 22 tranches, amounting to a 2.58% stake in Lenskart.
Technology investor SoftBank Group has once again trimmed its holding in Lenskart Solutions, selling nearly a 2.6% stake in the eyewear retailer for Rs 2,888 crore through open market transactions on Monday.
In June, SoftBank sold a 3.25% stake in Lenskart for Rs 2,873 crore.
In the latest transaction, Japan-based SoftBank Group, through its affiliate SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, offloaded 4.5 crore equity shares in 22 tranches, amounting to a 2.58% stake in Gurugram-based Lenskart, as per block deal data on the BSE.
The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 641.75 apiece, taking the combined deal size to Rs 2,887.87 crore.
The latest transaction brought SoftBank's holding in Lenskart down to 7.28% from 9.86%, although it remains the second-largest public shareholder in the eyewear firm.
Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an arm of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, remains the largest public shareholder of Lenskart with a 9.77% stake.
The block deal saw participation from a wide range of institutional investors.
Domestic buyers included National Pension System Trust and mutual funds managed by SBI, Edelweiss, Nippon India, Franklin Templeton, HDFC, HSBC, ICICI Prudential, Motilal Oswal and Sundaram. ICICI Prudential Life Insurance was also among the buyers.
Among foreign investors, financial services company Societe Generale picked up the most shares, acquiring 1,07,35,000 shares, representing a 0.62% stake.
The shares were bought at the same price, making the transaction worth Rs 688.91 crore.
Other foreign investors that lapped up shares of Lenskart included Ghisallo Capital Management, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Vanguard, Wasatch Global Investors, and Integrated Core Strategies Asia.
Other buyers included Frankfurt-based Universal Investment, the Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois, the Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System, and the Kuwait Investment Authority.
Shares of Lenskart Solutions fell 0.28% to close at Rs 659.70 apiece on the BSE.

input.title: Lenskart investors sell over $1 Bn stake in 3 months; SoftBank offloads another $300 Mn
input.content:
SoftBank has sold another 4.5 crore shares of eyewear retailer Lenskart for around Rs 2,888 crore (over $300 million) through a block deal, making its second large sell-off in the company since June.
According to the stock exchange, the shares were sold at Rs 641.75 each, taking the total value of the transaction to Rs 2,888 crore. SoftBank held 17.14 crore Lenskart shares, or a 9.69% stake, as of July. Following the latest sale, its holding has fallen to around 12.64 crore shares, or about 7.15%.
The latest transaction comes less than three months after SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth around Rs 2,873 crore in June. It had sold around 5.65 crore shares at Rs 508.55 each in that transaction.
SoftBank is not the only early investor to have reduced its stake in Lenskart in recent months. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) sold shares worth around Rs 1,960 crore in June, while Temasek offloaded shares worth around Rs 1,940 crore in July.
Together, these four transactions, including SoftBank's two sales, amount to around Rs 9,660 crore (over $1 billion) worth of Lenskart shares sold by large institutional investors since June.
The sell-offs come as Lenskart continues to see strong investor interest in the listed eyewear company. The company made its stock market debut in November 2025 and has since seen several large institutional transactions.
The latest block deal saw shares picked up by a mix of institutional investors, including Societe Generale, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Sundaram Mutual Fund and global funds.
During its latest quarterly results (Q1 FY27), the company posted 43% year-on-year growth in its revenue to Rs 2,714 crore with a profit of Rs 228 crore. The company closed its trading session at Rs 658.75, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,14,225 crore.

input.title: SoftBank Sells Lenskart Stake Worth ₹2,888 Cr
input.content: Adding to its Lenskart windfall, global investment firm SoftBank has now offloaded 4.50 Cr shares in the eyewear retailer to rake in ₹2,887.9 Cr. As per BSE data, the investor, via its holding entity SoftBank Vision Fund (SVF) II Lightbulb (Cayman) Ltd, sold the shares at an average price of ₹641.75 apiece, a 3% discount to the stock’s last closing price. This is the second major partial exit for SoftBank in Lenskart after the eyewear giant’s listing. Earlier in June, it sold shares worth 5.65 Cr shares in a block deal for ₹2,873.3 Cr. Despite the June stake sale, SoftBank held 9.79% stake or 17.14 Cr shares in the company at the end of June 31, 2026. European financial giant Societe Generale emerged as the single largest buyer, mopping up 1.1 Cr shares. Goldman Sachs secured 84.3 Lakh shares through two entities while Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund picked up 47.7 Lakh shares. Additionally, HSBC Mutual Fund bought 32.6 Lakh shares, while several investors linked with US investment firm Vanguard cumulatively bought 36.9 Lakh shares. HDFC Mutual Fund, Ghisallo Capital, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, and Kuwait Investment Authority were among the other major buyers who picked up some of the shares sold by SoftBank. The deal comes amid a significant bullish trajectory that the stock of the eyewear retailer has maintained in recent times. After a muted debut on the bourses in November, Lenskart’s shares have surged more than 69% from its listing price of ₹390. While the stock ended the day’s trading session 0.67% lower at ₹656.95, it has zoomed by about 50% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The bull run has allowed other institutional backers — KKR, ABG Capital, Alpha Wave, TR Capital, ADIA — to pare stake in the eyewear major since lock-in expiry on May 8. The strong movement of the new-age tech company has been supported by its improvement bottom line position since listing. Lenskart achieved its maiden full-year profitability in FY25 and saw its net profit more than double to ₹530 Cr in FY26 while registering a 32.3% uptick in revenue to ₹9,002.3 Cr. In Q1 FY27, its bottom line more than tripled YoY to ₹228.4 Cr while operating revenue jumped 43% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹2,714.2 Cr. While announcing its results, Lenskart also disclosed a series of investments to bolster its international businesses. These included a ₹10.6 Cr in Singapore-based Baofeng Framekart Technology Ltd, a JV between subsidiary Lenskart Solutions Pte Ltd and Geng Yongchao, a ₹20 Cr towards expanding its step-down subsidiary, OWNDAYS, into the Republic of Korea and setting up a new step-down subsidiary in China. However, in a separate development, Lenskart reported a cyber incident that affected a sub-vendor of its Singapore-based group company earlier last week.

input.title: Yahoo Finance
input.content:
New Positioning Establishes Company's Addressable Market as a Lifecycle Engineering Services Company and Reinforces Focus on Exemplary Outcomes
HYDERABAD, India, Aug. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cyient today unveiled its new brand positioning and promise, 'Nothing Less,' reflecting its evolution as a Global Lifecycle Engineering Services leader and its commitment to helping customers achieve exemplary outcomes in an increasingly complex, intelligence-driven world. The refreshed positioning brings intelligent engineering to every stage of the lifecycle, combining deep engineering expertise, domain knowledge, human intelligence, and AI applied in context.
The new positioning will be the focal point of Cyient's go-to-market strategy, representing an engineering portfolio that partners with customers across the full life cycle of their products and the assets that power their businesses, creating value measured over decades rather than projects.
The new brand reflects both the company's capability and ways of working. Intelligent Engineering defines what we do: bringing together engineering, digital, and industry expertise to help customers improve performance, reliability, and growth. Embracing Intelligence defines how we do it: harnessing the combined power of people, data, and AI to unlock better decisions and better outcomes. Together, they reinforce Cyient's focus on delivering exemplary outcomes.
Krishna Bodanapu, Executive Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Cyient, said, "Since our founding in 1991, Cyient has partnered with some of the world's leading organizations to solve complex engineering challenges and deliver outcomes that matter. We have, over the years, built deep domain expertise across the industries and earned the trust of customers operating in some of the most demanding and mission-critical environments. This legacy of engineering excellence, customer focus, and value-driven ownership has shaped who we are today and sets the foundation for our next phase of growth."
Commenting on the new positioning, Sukamal Banerjee, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Cyient Ltd, said, "Nothing Less is a reflection of how Cyient has evolved and where we are headed. As a Global Lifecycle Engineering Services company, we are expanding the value we deliver across the entire life of an asset, from design to manufacture to services. Competitive advantage today comes from the convergence of engineering expertise, human ingenuity, and AI-driven intelligence. Cyient brings these strengths together in a unique way. We help customers solve complex challenges faster, improve outcomes, and unlock greater value throughout the lifecycle."

input.title: Block deals today: Meesho, Lenskart shares to see action; likely selling shareholders, targets
input.content:
Meesho Ltd and Lenskart Solutions Ltd are in focus on Monday morning as both stocks are likely to see block deals. SoftBank entity SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman) is looking to sell a 2.6 per cent stake, or 4.5 crore shares, in Lenskart Solutions, raising around $300 million, according to the term sheet. Meesho, meanwhile, could see Y Combinator offload shares worth $100 million, or 4.85 crore shares representing a 1.05 per cent stake, according to a report.
The floor price for the Meesho block deal has been set at Rs 197.50 per share, a 4 per cent discount to its previous close, Bloomberg reported. The floor price for the Lenskart deal has been fixed at Rs 635 per share, around 4 per cent below its Friday closing price on the BSE.
Goldman Sachs is the sole placing agent for the Lenskart deal, while Kotak Securities is handling the Meesho transaction.
Meesho target prices
Meesho has eight 'Buy' ratings, three 'Hold' calls and three 'Sell' ratings. Its 12-month Bloomberg consensus target at Rs 205.77, however, suggests nil upside potential. Axis Capital was the latest brokerage with updates on the company. The brokerage on August 18 suggested a 'Buy' and a target of Rs 230 on the stock. Macquarie has on August 5 suggested 'Underperform' wwith a target of Rs 125, the lowest on the Street. MOFSL has 'Buy' on the stock with a target of Rs 240. HSBC has 'Hold' with a target of Rs 185.
Lenskart target prices
In the case of Lenskart, there are 18 'Buy' calls, three 'Hold' calls and one 'Sell' call. Yet its 12-month Bloomberg consensus target at Rs 672.24 suggests a mere 1.6 per cent potential upside. Macquarie on August 21 suggested 'Outperform' on the stock with a target of Rs 700. ICICI Securities on the same day suggested 'Buy' and a target of Rs 750 on the stock. UBS has the highest target of Rs 800, while Ambit's Rs 496 is the lowest, Bloomberg data showed.
 ICICI Securities in a fresh note said Lenskart has turned a strong start into a sustained run, delivering over 50 per cent returns since its market debut. The company’s sustained operational outperformance remains the centrepiece of this rerating story, it said.
"We think investors would now focus on Lenskart’s ability to sustain such growth and the rationale behind the rich valuations. We estimate Lenskart’s India business to deliver a revenue CAGR of 23 per cent over FY26–31E, as we expect its store count to almost treble (2.7x) with SSSG of ~18% over the same period. Further, scale efficiencies could support an EBITDA CAGR of ~37% in India business over the same period," it said on Monday.
"We upgrade our pre-IndAS EBITDA estimate by 10-11% for FY27E/28E/29E to factor in better sales growth and higher margins in the international business. We maintain Buy with a higher target of Rs 690 (from Rs 615) on March ’28E EV/pre-IndAS EBITDA of 50x (unchanged)," Equirus Securities said in a recent note.

input.title: Sun Pharma recalls over 1900 bottles of epilepsy drug in US
input.content:
- Pharma Industry
- 1 min read
Sun Pharma recalls over 1900 bottles of epilepsy drug in US
                    According to the US FDA’s latest enforcement report, the recall was initiated after black spots were found on the tablets due to burnt excipient used for manufacturing.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        New Delhi: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is undertaking a voluntary recall of “1968 bottles” anticonvulsant therapy, “carbamazepine” in the US.
According to the US FDA’s latest enforcement report, the recall was initiated after black spots were found on the tablets due to burnt excipient used for manufacturing.
Sun Pharma initiated the recall on August 3 following a complaint about black specks found in tablets. The company later identified cGMP deviations as the underlying cause of the issue.
The affected batch was manufactured at Taro Pharmaceutical’s (wholly-owned subsidiary of Sun Pharma) Haifa Bay-based facility in israel.
Carbamazepine is an anti-seizure therapy which is used to treat epilepsy, nerve pain like trigeminal neuralgia, and bipolar disorders.
The nationwide rollback is classified as a “call II” recall by the FDA, meaning that the products may cause temporary or reversible adverse health consequences. However the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote.

USFDA approves Jubilant’s new line
Jubilant Pharmova Ltd has informed the exchanges that the US drug regulator, USFDA, has approved the commercial batch manufacturing of the first product on the new Isolator-based fill-and-finish line, Line 3, of Jubilant HollisterStier LLC (JHS)’s contract manufacturing facility located in Spokane, WA. US. Jubilant HollisterStier LLC is a subsidiary of Jubilant Pharma Holding Inc., which is a subsidiary of Jubilant Pharma Limited, Singapore, a wholly owned subsidiary of the company.
Caplin Steriles gets 10 USFDA observations
Caplin Point Laboratories has announced the completion of an unannounced inspection by the United States Food and Drug Administration at the manufacturing facility of its subsidiary, Caplin Steriles Limited. The inspection was conducted at the company’s injectable and ophthalmic manufacturing plant in Gummidipoondi, spanning August 13 to 21, 2026. At the conclusion of the audit, the US regulatory authority issued a Form 483 containing 10 observations. Caplin Point Laboratories clarified that all 10 observations are strictly procedural.
Natco Pharma, Choksi Labs receive USFDA observations
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a Form 483 with four observations to Natco Pharma after inspecting the generic drugmaker’s finished dosage formulations (FDF) unit in Visakhapatnam. The inspection was conducted from August 17 to 21, and the company said it believes the observations are procedural. Similarly, the US FDA inspected Choksi Laboratories Ltd’s central laboratory in Indore and concluded the inspection with four observations. On conclusion of the inspection, the Company received 4 (Four) observations. We are addressing the observations comprehensively and will respond to the USFDA within the stipulated timeframe.
Power Grid bags ₹822.91-crore order
Power Grid Corporation of India has secured a confirmed work order valued at ₹822.91 crore per annum through Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB). The contract covers the development of a transmission system to integrate power from Renewable Energy Projects in Jam Khambhaliya REZ in Gujarat - Phase II (5,500 MW) and Jamnagar Phase-I (1,000 MW), totalling 6,500 MW of capacity. The project is awarded on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) basis.
NTPC Renewable Energy wins 500 MW bid
NTPC Renewable Energy Limited (NTPC REL), a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC Green Energy Limited, has emerged as a successful bidder in the e-reverse auction conducted by SECI for Selection of RE Power Developers for Assured Peak Supply of 6000 MWh (1500 MW x 4 Hrs.) from ISTS-Connected RE Projects in India, under Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (SECI-FDRE-IX). Under the terms of the Request for Selection (RfS), NTPC Renewable Energy has secured 500 MW contracted capacity at a discovered tariff of ₹6/kWh.
Diamond Power gets ₹52.86-crore cable order
Diamond Power Infrastructure Ltd has received a Letter of Intent (LOI) from Aurionpro Solutions Ltd for the supply of HT and LT electrical cables to a hyperscale data centre campus at Hyderabad. The LOI, valued at approximately ₹52.86 crore (Including GST), covers the HYD-20 package of the campus, for which Aurionpro is the appointed EPC contractor. Supplies commence immediately and are scheduled on a staggered basis in line with the site’s construction programme, delivered DAP Hyderabad. The contract is on a price-variation basis under the IEEMA formula with April 2026 base indices.
NGT dismisses challenges to GHCL project clearances
GHCL Ltd has informed the exchange that the National Green Tribunal’s (NGT) Western Zone Bench in Pune has dismissed all three appeals challenging the environmental and forest clearances for its greenfield soda ash project in Gujarat.
Kaynes Technology signs MoU with BOSGAME
Kaynes Technology India Ltd and BOSGAME have signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), marking an important step towards establishing and expanding BOSGAME’s presence in the Indian market. The collaboration brings together BOSGAME’s product innovation and intelligent computing portfolio with Kaynes Technology’s extensive capabilities in electronics design, engineering, integrated manufacturing, testing, supply chain management, and lifecycle support.
Craftsman Automation plans Germany entity
The board of Craftsman Automation has approved a proposal to incorporate Craftsman Fronberg Precision GmbH in Germany by Craftsman Germany GmbH, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, subject to completion of statutory and regulatory formalities and such approvals as may be required under applicable laws. The proposed entity is being incorporated to undertake machining and processing activities related to engine and engineering components. The incorporation is intended to support the development of in-house machining capabilities, strengthen operational flexibility, and support the future growth of the Group’s operations in Germany.
Ceinsys Tech loses ₹112.42-crore orders
Ceinsys Tech Ltd has issued an operational update regarding its ongoing work orders with the State Water and Sanitation Mission (SWSM), Water Supply and Sanitation Department (WSSD), Government of Maharashtra, revealing cancellation of Rs 112.42 crore worth orders. The disclosure follows previous announcements made on October 22, 2023, and October 9, 2024, concerning Letters of Award valued at Rs. 248.39 crore and Rs. 331.61 crore, respectively. These contracts pertained to the appointment of System Integrators for IoT deployment-encompassing design, implementation, and maintenance alongside a centralised IoT platform-for Jal Jeevan Mission Projects in Maharashtra. WSM informed Ceinsys Tech that because the sanctioned implementation funds for IoT under allocated MJP MVS schemes have been exhausted, the allocation for 617 ZP schemes stands cancelled. This cancellation results in an overall reduction of Rs. 112.42 crore in the value of the company’s pending executable orders, it said.
Refex Industries expands senior leadership
Refex Industries has announced changes to its senior executive team. As part of this leadership expansion, Anil S. Kulkarni has been appointed and designated as the Chief Business Officer for the Ready-Mix Concrete (RMC) Division within the Ash & Coal Handling Business Unit. Concurrently, Prasad Jakkaraju has been designated as Senior Management Personnel to serve as Vice President and Head of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) within the ESG & EHS department.
Acutaas Chemicals approves ₹212-crore capex
The board of directors of Acutaas Chemicals Ltd has approved a substantial capital expenditure plan of up to Rs. 212 crore, earmarked for establishing a new greenfield or brownfield manufacturing plant in the state of Gujarat.
