input.title: Siliconindia Magazine
input.content:
Nykaa Acquires 51 Percent Stake in Skincare Brand Aminu for Rs 32 Crore
    
          
            By
              siliconindia  |  Wednesday, 05 August 2026, 10:55 IST 
                                                                                         
        
                
      
	Nykaa has approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in premium D2C skincare brand Aminu for up to Rs 32 crore. The deal will strengthen Nykaa’s owned beauty portfolio and expand its presence in the premium skincare segment.
	Beauty and personal care platform Nykaa is expanding its premium skincare portfolio by acquiring a majority stake in direct-to-consumer (D2C) skincare brand Aminu. Nykaa’s board has approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu for a cash consideration of up to Rs 32 crore.
	According to exchange filings, the transaction is expected to be completed by September 15. Nykaa also plans to acquire the remaining 49% stake in Aminu over the next few years.
	The founders of Aminu will continue to manage the company’s operations, while Nykaa will support the brand’s growth by leveraging its platform, distribution network, and market reach.
	Founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, Aminu offers premium skincare products, including serums, cleansers, sunscreens, masks, moisturizers, and body care products. The brand currently has over 60 stock-keeping units (SKUs) and also provides personalized skin consultation services.
	Aminu operates in the premium skincare category, a segment where Nykaa is looking to expand its presence. The company said Aminu’s products have a higher price point compared with several existing brands under the Nykaa portfolio, helping it fill a gap in the premium skincare market.
	The acquisition will also help Nykaa strengthen its in-house skincare capabilities. Aminu has more than 30 proprietary formulations and focuses on research and development-driven products.
	The brand’s omnichannel presence was another factor behind Nykaa’s investment decision. Aminu sells products through its own website, beauty platforms such as Nykaa and Clinikally, e-commerce marketplaces including Amazon and Zepto, and is also available across 180 salons in India.
	The D2C brand has recorded strong growth in recent years. Aminu reported revenue of Rs 19.4 crore in FY26, registering a nearly 50% increase from around Rs 13 crore in FY25.
	According to Aminu, the brand sources ingredients from more than 40 countries and uses over 250 ingredients across its product range. It focuses on clean skincare formulations and claims to have removed nearly 3,000 commonly used ingredients from its products.
	The acquisition aligns with Nykaa’s broader strategy of building its 'House of Brands' portfolio across different beauty categories and price segments. In the past, Nykaa has acquired or invested in beauty brands such as Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm as part of this strategy.
	Currently, Nykaa’s portfolio includes seven beauty and personal care brands and five fashion brands, including its own Nykaa Cosmetics line. The company plans to continue expanding into categories such as premium fragrances, mid-premium nutraceuticals, derma skincare, and professional makeup products.
	The deal comes alongside Nykaa reporting strong financial performance for the first quarter of FY27. The company posted a more than threefold increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 79.8 crore, compared with Rs 24.8 crore in the same quarter last year. Its operating revenue rose 29% year-on-year to Rs 2,782 crore.
	Following the announcement, Nykaa shares closed 0.85% higher at Rs 344.80.
	With this acquisition, Nykaa is strengthening its position in India’s growing premium beauty market while supporting the expansion of homegrown skincare brands.

input.title: Nykaa shares pare gains after hitting 52-week high; here’s what Jefferies, Nomura, other analysts said on Q1 FY27 earnings
input.content:
Market News
4 min read | Updated on August 05, 2026, 12:29 IST
SUMMARY
Nykaa reported a 247% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27).
Stock list
FSN E-Commerce Ventures shares tumbled 6% from their 52-week high level to an intraday low of ₹327.7 apiece. Image: Shutterstock.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures shares tumbled 6% from their 52-week high level to an intraday low of ₹327.7 apiece. At the time of writing the piece, the stock was trading at ₹336.3 apiece on the National Stock Exchange, declining 1.81%.
Nykaa reported a 247% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27). In the corresponding quarter last year, the beauty and personal care retailer had posted a net profit of ₹23 crore.
The company’s revenue from operations increased 29% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹2,782 crore as compared to ₹2,155 crore in Q1 FY26.
On the operational level, Nykaa’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at ₹236 crore, marking a jump of 69% from ₹140 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. The company’s EBITDA margin also expanded to 8.4% in contrast to 6.5% YoY.
Nykaa’s beauty vertical GMV for Q1 FY27 stood at ₹4,105 crore. This includes performance across businesses of e-commerce, retail stores, eB2B distribution and the House of Nykaa Beauty portfolio. NSV growth came in at 29% YoY this quarter, accelerating from the mid-20s growth recorded over the past few quarters.
As India's largest beauty specialty retail network, the company expanded its beauty retail footprint to 324 stores across 105 cities, with total retail space increasing 29% YoY to ~3.3 lakh sq. ft.
Along with the earnings, Nykaa also said it acquired 51% stake in Aminu Wellness Private Limited, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand, for a total consideration of ₹32 crore.
“This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters. Our AI-led initiatives are beginning to create meaningful consumer experiences, with Virtual Closet already driving 2x higher conversion and AskNykaa, our conversational search engine, emerging as a trusted beauty advisor on the platform,” said Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa.
Analysts from HSBC said FSN E-Commerce’s GMV performance remained robust, with the beauty and personal care (BPC) segment growing 28% and the fashion segment rising 53%. The analysts also noted that the company’s House of Brands continues to scale up.
They further highlighted that the EBITDA margin expanded by around 195 basis points year-on-year, marking the third consecutive quarter of over 150 basis points expansion, indicating that operating leverage is beginning to reflect.
Nomura analysts said growth is accelerating at FSN E-Commerce, with margin levers starting to play out. The analysts noted that EBITDA for Q1 FY27 came in ahead of consensus estimates, supported by premiumisation trends and AI-driven efficiencies.

input.title: Nykaa acquires 51% stake in skincare brand Aminu for ₹32 crore
input.content:
ADVERTISEMENT
Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa will acquire a 51% stake in Mumbai-based skincare brand Aminu for ₹32 crore through an all-cash transaction, according to a stock exchange filing.
Nykaa said Aminu operates in a high-growth segment of the beauty market and has emerged as one of the top premium skincare brands on its platform in the ₹1,000-₹1,900 price range. The brand sells products including serums and sleep oils.
Founded in 2019, Aminu is a bootstrapped skincare startup. The company reported revenue of ₹19.5 crore in FY26, up from ₹13 crore a year earlier, reflecting growing demand for premium skincare products in India.
According to Nykaa, spending in India's beauty and personal care market continues to be concentrated in the premium segment. The company said Aminu's positioning, research and development capabilities and omnichannel presence make it a good fit within its beauty portfolio.
The acquisition adds another brand to Nykaa's expanding stable of owned and partner-led beauty businesses. Under its House of Nykaa portfolio, the company already operates and invests in brands such as Kay Beauty, Dot & Key and Nykaa Cosmetics.
The deal announcement came alongside Nykaa's June-quarter earnings. Parent company FSN E-Commerce Ventures reported a net profit of ₹80 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with ₹24 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore.
Nykaa's beauty business continued to be the company's key growth driver during the quarter. The beauty segment's net sales value grew 29% year-on-year, supported by growth across e-commerce, physical retail stores and owned brands.
The acquisition also reflects increased consolidation in India's beauty and skincare market, where larger platforms are investing in niche premium brands to strengthen product portfolios and deepen customer engagement. Premium skincare has been one of the fastest-growing categories in the sector, driven by higher consumer spending, social commerce and growing awareness around skincare routines.
According to reports, Nykaa may acquire the remaining stake in Aminu over the next few years, while the founders are expected to continue leading the business. The first phase of the transaction is expected to close during the September quarter.

input.title: Nykaa’s Q1 Snapshot, Klassroom Wraps Up IPO & More
input.content: Nykaa’s Stellar Q1 Nykaa fired on all cylinders in Q1. The quarter saw the beauty ecommerce giant clock a three-fold jump in profits, expand margins and increase its footprint. Meanwhile, its fashion business turned EBITDA positive for the first time. Here is a snapshot of Nykaa’s Q1 FY27 numbers: Net profit zoomed 3X YoY to ₹79.8 Cr Operating revenue rose 29% YoY to ₹2,782 Cr Total expenses also grew 26% YoY to ₹2,662 Cr EBITDA grew 68% YoY to ₹236 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 8.5% The Beauty Upside: Powered by stronger engagement, improving margins, higher average order values and a premium portfolio, the beauty business remained Nykaa’s core engine. The vertical contributed 90% of its total revenue in Q1. The quarter also saw Nykaa Beauty deepen its omnichannel footprint to 324 stores, while onboarding global names to broaden choice. The Fashion Fiesta: Nykaa Fashion turned EBITDA positive for the first time on the back of stronger operating leverage. The business also managed to accelerate GMV and net sales on the back of a wider brand mix and sharper merchandising. Expansions into activewear, kidswear and footwear also helped Nykaa’s fashion arm move from a growth bet to a serious contender. The Q-Comm Mania: The quarter also saw Nykaa scale its quick commerce platform to 13 cities, with a target to cross 25 by end-FY27. While domestic consumption remained strong, Nykaa’s Gulf joint venture, Nysaa, continued to face pressures due to geopolitical tensions. This dampened overseas acceleration. The House Of Brands: Premiumisation push also remained high on the beauty giant’s agenda. Nykaa now plans to acquire a 51% stake in D2C skincare brand Aminu to fill the gap in its premium skincare portfolio and leverage the brand’s salon distribution. Together with earlier buys like Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm, Nykaa appears to be reinforcing its house of brands strategy across categories and price points. As the beauty ecommerce major finally marries scale with profitability, here is how Nykaa fared on the financial front in Q1… From The Editor’s Desk 🎓 Klassroom Wraps Up IPO The edtech platform’s public issue was oversubscribed 146% on the third and final day of bidding, receiving bids for 25.66 Lakh shares against 17.58 Lakh shares on offer. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has announced that CRISIL Ratings has removed the ‘Rating Watch with Developing Implications’ status from the company’s long-term bank facilities. The top-tier rating of ‘CRISIL AAA’ has been reaffirmed with a stable outlook. This follows an earlier communication on May 7, 2026, where the rating was placed under watch. Credit Rating Update for Sun Pharma
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited today announced an update on its credit rating. Following a review, CRISIL Ratings Limited has removed the ‘Rating Watch with Developing Implications’ status that was previously placed on the company’s long-term bank facilities.
Reaffirmation of ‘CRISIL AAA/Stable’ Rating
The agency has reaffirmed the rating assigned to Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited’s long-term bank facilities at the highest category, ‘CRISIL AAA’. Crucially, the rating now carries a ‘Stable’ outlook. This reassures investors about the company’s robust financial health and its ability to meet its financial obligations.
Background of the Rating Watch
This development is in reference to a prior communication dated 07 May 2026. This action was triggered by the company’s announcement on 27 April 2026, the implications of which have now been assessed, leading to the removal of the watch and the stable outlook.

input.title: Nykaa Q1FY27 Net Profit Surges 226% to ₹80 Crore on Strong Revenue Growth
input.content:
Nykaa Q1FY27 Net Profit Surges 226% to ₹80 Crore on Strong Revenue Growth
Nykaa reported a 226% YoY jump in Q1FY27 net profit to ₹80 crore, with revenue up 29% to ₹2,782 crore and EBITDA rising 68% to ₹236 crore at an 8.5% margin — the highest in 12 quarters. The fashion segment turned EBITDA positive, and Nykaa acquired a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness to strengthen its premium skincare portfolio.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, operating as Nykaa, reported a significant surge in profitability for the first quarter of FY27, driven by accelerated revenue growth and margin expansion. The company's consolidated net profit after tax (PAT) rose 226% year-on-year to ₹80 crore, up from ₹23.3 crore in Q1FY26. This sharp improvement in bottom-line performance reflects enhanced operational efficiency and scale across its beauty and fashion verticals.
Financial Performance Highlights
Nykaa's total revenue from operations grew 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore in Q1FY27, compared to ₹2,155 crore in the corresponding period last year. Gross profit expanded by 33% to ₹1,276 crore, while EBITDA increased by 68% to ₹236 crore. The EBITDA margin widened to 8.5% from 6.5% a year ago, marking the highest level in the past 12 quarters. Consolidated gross merchandise value (GMV) also climbed 34% to ₹5,590 crore.
The improvement in EBITDA margins indicates that Nykaa has successfully scaled its business while managing costs more effectively. Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson and CEO, attributed this to disciplined execution and innovation-led consumer experiences.
Business Verticals Update
The Beauty vertical remained the core driver, with GMV reaching ₹4,105 crore and net sales value (NSV) growing 29% year-on-year. Key launches included Rare Beauty, SK-II, and Judydoll, strengthening the premium portfolio. Nykaa Fashion delivered a standout performance with GMV rising 53% to ₹1,471 crore and NSV increasing 54% to ₹451 crore. Notably, the fashion segment turned EBITDA positive, achieving a 0.1% margin compared to a -6.2% margin in Q1FY26.
Acquisition of Aminu Wellness
In a strategic move to expand its House of Nykaa portfolio, Nykaa acquired a 51% majority stake in Aminu Wellness Private Limited. Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, has grown revenues eightfold over three years to reach ₹19 crore in FY26. The brand is profitable and known for its science-first approach and proprietary formulations. Post-acquisition, the founders will continue to manage operations, with Nykaa planning to acquire the remaining stake over the next few years on pre-agreed terms. This deal reinforces Nykaa's leadership in the premium skincare segment by integrating Aminu's R&D capabilities with Nykaa's omnichannel reach.
What the Numbers Show
The divergence between revenue growth (29%) and net profit growth (226%) highlights a significant leverage effect from operational efficiencies. With EBITDA margins hitting a 12-quarter high at 8.5%, Nykaa is demonstrating that its scale is translating into meaningful profitability rather than just top-line expansion. The turn to positive EBITDA in the fashion segment further signals improving unit economics across key growth drivers.

input.title: Nykaa Q1 Results: Falguni Nayar-Led FSN E-Com Profit Soars Over 3x, Revenue Climbs 29% on Strong Beauty Demand
input.content:
Nykaa Q1 Results: Falguni Nayar-Led FSN E-Com Profit Soars Over 3x, Revenue Climbs 29% on Strong Beauty Demand
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, delivered a strong start to FY27, reporting a sharp jump in profitability for the June quarter as robust demand across its beauty business, improving operating efficiency and continued expansion of its omnichannel network supported overall performance.
Nykaa Q1 Results: FSN E-Commerce Ventures Reports Triple Profit on Strong Revenue Growth
Led by founder and Executive Chairperson Falguni Nayar, the company recorded healthy double-digit growth in revenue while significantly improving margins, highlighting continued momentum despite a challenging consumption environment. The latest earnings also reflect Nykaa's ongoing focus on expanding its physical retail footprint and strengthening its quick-commerce presence across the country.
For the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), Nykaa reported a net profit of Rs 79.76 crore, more than three times higher than the Rs 24.47 crore posted in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, profit remained largely stable after the company had reported Rs 78 crore in the March quarter, indicating that the retailer was able to sustain its improved profitability despite continued investments in business expansion.
Revenue Climbs Nearly 30% on Strong Consumer Demand
The Mumbai-headquartered beauty and fashion retailer reported revenue from operations of Rs 2,782 crore, registering a 29% year-on-year increase from Rs 2,155 crore in the same quarter last year. Revenue also improved sequentially from Rs 2,648 crore reported in the previous quarter, reflecting sustained customer demand across Nykaa's beauty, personal care and fashion platforms.
The strong top-line performance indicates that consumer spending remained resilient during the quarter, with the company continuing to benefit from its premium product portfolio, growing online customer base and expanding offline presence.
Nykaa Gross Profit and EBITDA Hit Multi-Quarter Highs
Nykaa delivered a notable improvement in operating performance during the June quarter. Gross profit increased 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,276 crore, while EBITDA rose 68% compared with the same period last year to Rs 236 crore.
The company's EBITDA margin expanded to 8.5%, up from 6.5% a year earlier, marking its highest operating margin in the past 12 quarters. The improvement suggests that Nykaa continued to enhance operational efficiency while maintaining healthy sales growth across its businesses.
Expenses Rise Alongside Business Expansion
As the company continued investing in growth initiatives, its overall expenditure also increased during the quarter. Total expenses stood at Rs 2,662.15 crore, compared with Rs 2,120.56 crore in the year-ago period and Rs 2,535.80 crore in the previous quarter.
The higher spending largely reflects continued investments in expanding retail operations, technology infrastructure, logistics capabilities and customer acquisition as Nykaa scales its omnichannel ecosystem.
Nykaa Expands Store Network Across India
The company continued to strengthen its offline presence during the June quarter by opening new retail stores across multiple cities. Nykaa's beauty retail network expanded to 324 stores spread across 105 cities, while its total retail area increased 29% year-on-year to approximately 3.3 lakh square feet.
The expansion forms part of the company's broader omnichannel strategy, which combines its digital platform with a growing network of physical stores to enhance customer experience and improve product accessibility across India.
Nykaa Now Quick-Commerce Business Accelerates Expansion
Nykaa also continued scaling its quick-commerce platform, Nykaa Now, as consumer demand for faster deliveries gained momentum. The service is currently operational in 13 cities, and the company plans to extend its reach to more than 25 cities by the end of FY27.

input.title: Nykaa Q1 Results: Net profit surges over threefold to  ₹80 crore on strong beauty demand
input.content:
Nykaa's parent, FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd., reported a more than three-fold jump in its June quarter profit, driven by strong growth in its beauty business and a sharp acceleration in fashion sales, while improved cost efficiencies boosted its operating performance. The company posted a 226% year-on-year (YoY) jump in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore in the April-June quarter, according to its regulatory filing released on Tuesday. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 29% YoY to ₹2,782 crore during the quarter. At the operating level, EBITDA increased 68% YoY to ₹236 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded 200 basis points to 8%. The strong quarterly performance was primarily driven by sustained demand for skincare and makeup products. Revenue from the beauty segment rose 27.4% YoY to ₹2,516 crore in the June quarter. The beauty vertical's gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 28% YoY to ₹4,105 crore, supported by continued momentum across its e-commerce platform, offline retail network, and owned brands under the House of Nykaa portfolio. Meanwhile, net sales value (NSV) increased 29% YoY, accelerating from the mid-20% growth recorded over the past few quarters. House of Nykaa continued its strong growth trajectory, achieving an annualised GMV run rate of around ₹3,758 crore, reflecting 39% YoY growth. The portfolio reported NSV of ₹550 crore in the quarter, up 36% YoY, while expanding its customer base to more than 18 million, highlighting strong consumer demand and continued brand adoption. Nykaa's fashion business also delivered a strong performance during the quarter, with GMV rising 53% YoY to ₹1,471 crore, while NSV increased 54% YoY to ₹451 crore. The segment also reported a meaningful improvement in profitability, with the EBITDA margin (as a percentage of NSV) improving to 0.1% from 6.2% in the year-ago quarter. According to the company, the growth was supported by strong customer additions, with the cumulative customer base expanding 34% YoY to 12 million. The company also strengthened its brand portfolio and strategic partnerships, including Nike and H&M, which continued to support the segment's growth. Momentum remained broad-based across both core and emerging categories. Women's fashion grew 40% YoY, while men's fashion surged 83% and kidswear rose 57%. During the quarter, the company said it added more than 130 new brands, including Birkenstock, Debenhams, and H&M Move, further strengthening its product offerings. Meanwhile, its partnership with Nike continued to gain traction, with the Nike app crossing 1.5 million installs within six months of launch, making it one of the top three brands on Nykaa's platforms. input.title: Nykaa Q1 profit more than triples as revenue climbs 29%; fashion business turns EBITDA positive
input.content:
Nykaa Q1 profit more than triples as revenue climbs 29%; fashion business turns EBITDA positive
ADVERTISEMENT
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd., the parent company of Nykaa, reported a sharp rise in first-quarter profit, driven by robust growth in its core beauty business and continued improvement in operational efficiency, while its fashion business turned EBITDA positive during the quarter.
The company reported revenue from operations of ₹2,782 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up 29.1% from ₹2,154.9 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Profit after tax jumped to ₹79.8 crore from ₹24.5 crore a year ago, while profit before tax nearly tripled to ₹129.2 crore from ₹43.7 crore.
At the operating level, EBITDA rose 67.8% year-on-year to ₹236.1 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding to 8.5% from 6.5% in the year-ago period, reflecting improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management. Finance costs declined to ₹26.7 crore from ₹30.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Beauty business remains the growth engine
Nykaa said its Beauty vertical continued to deliver strong momentum during the quarter, supported by healthy customer demand, premiumisation trends and expansion across owned brands and retail channels. The company also continued to deepen its omnichannel presence through physical stores while strengthening its online platform.
The Fashion business maintained its recovery trajectory and achieved EBITDA positivity, aided by improved assortment, better inventory management and greater operating efficiencies, marking another step towards sustainable profitability.
Management highlights profitable growth
Founder, executive chairperson and CEO Falguni Nayar said the company continued to execute its strategy of balancing growth with profitability.
"Our focus remains on building a sustainable and profitable business while continuing to invest in customer experience, technology and our brands. The strong performance this quarter reflects healthy consumer demand and disciplined execution across our businesses," she said.
The company also announced that its board has approved the acquisition of a 51% equity stake in Aminu Wellness Pvt. Ltd. for a consideration of up to ₹32 crore, expanding Nykaa's presence in the wellness segment.
Nykaa said it will continue to invest in brand building, technology capabilities and omnichannel expansion as it seeks to strengthen its leadership position in India's beauty and lifestyle market while improving profitability across businesses.
Shares of FSN E-Commerce Ventures ended 0.70% lower at ₹342.50 apiece on the NSE on Tuesday. The stock has surged over 60% during the past year, outperforming the Nifty Midcap 50 index, which has gained nearly 13% over the same period.

input.title: Nykaa Q1 profit jumps 227 per cent as revenue nears Rs 2,800 crore
input.content:
Brands
Nykaa Q1 profit jumps 227 per cent as revenue nears Rs 2,800 crore
Marketing spend rises to Rs 412 crore as beauty retailer balances growth with profitability
MUMBAI: Beauty may be skin deep, but Nykaa’s latest numbers suggest the real glow-up is happening on the balance sheet. With bigger marketing bets and sharper margins, the beauty retailer is proving that spending to grow doesn’t have to come at the cost of profits.
Nykaa, operated by FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, kicked off FY27 with robust top-line growth and a sharp improvement in profitability, even as it stepped up investments in advertising and customer acquisition to strengthen its position in India’s fast-growing beauty and fashion e-commerce market.
For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of Rs 2,782 crore, up 29 per cent from Rs 2,155 crore a year earlier and 5 per cent higher than Rs 2,648 crore in the previous quarter.
Gross profit rose 33 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,276 crore, with gross margins expanding to 45.9 per cent, compared with 44.6 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year and 45.4 per cent in the March quarter.
Marketing remained one of the company’s biggest areas of investment. Advertising, marketing and selling & distribution expenditure increased 26 per cent year-on-year to Rs 412 crore, up from Rs 328 crore in the year-ago quarter and 8 per cent higher than the Rs 380 crore spent in the preceding quarter.
Despite the increased spending, marketing costs became more efficient relative to revenue. Marketing expenditure accounted for 14.8 per cent of revenue, lower than 15.2 per cent a year ago, although marginally higher than 14.4 per cent in the previous quarter, indicating that revenue growth continued to outpace promotional investments.
Nykaa also delivered stronger operating performance. Contribution profit climbed 37 per cent year-on-year to Rs 589 crore, while the contribution margin improved to 21.2 per cent, compared with 19.9 per cent a year earlier.
EBITDA surged 68 per cent to Rs 236 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding by 196 basis points to 8.5 per cent, up from 6.5 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, EBITDA increased 3 per cent from Rs 223 crore, while margins edged up from 8.4 per cent.
At the bottom line, profit after tax (PAT) jumped 227 per cent year-on-year to Rs 80 crore, compared with Rs 24 crore in the same quarter last year. Sequentially, profit remained largely stable against Rs 79 crore reported in the March quarter.
Profit before tax nearly tripled to Rs 129 crore, while the PAT margin improved to 2.9 per cent, up from 1.1 per cent a year earlier.
Commenting on the performance, Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa, said crossing the US$1 billion annual revenue milestone while maintaining profitability and capital efficiency marked a defining moment in the company’s 14-year journey.
She noted that over the past three years, Nykaa has evolved into a multi-engine growth platform, with its Beauty and Fashion businesses doubling their gross merchandise value (GMV), while newer verticals such as Superstore and House of Nykaa have grown four-fold during the same period.
The company now serves more than 55 million consumers, with Nayar highlighting artificial intelligence as a key enabler for improving personalisation, operational efficiency and scalability across its businesses. She also identified wellness as Nykaa’s next major growth frontier alongside its core beauty and fashion operations.
The strong quarterly performance builds on FY26, when Nykaa crossed the US$1 billion annual revenue mark, reporting Rs 10,022 crore in revenue, 59 per cent growth in EBITDA and 183 per cent growth in net profit, making it the company’s strongest full-year profitability performance to date.

GMV in the fashion business segment rose 53% year-on-year to Rs 1,471 crore, and net sales value grew 54% to Rs 451 crore.
Nykaa Now, the company’s quick-delivery service, expanded to 13 cities during the quarter and is expected to reach more than 25 cities by the end of FY2027, offering over 1,000 marquee brands with delivery in 30-60 minutes.

This also marks our first full quarter of operating nike.in in India, which has led to meaningful increase to our already growing fashion business. Our AI-led initiatives are beginning to create meaningful consumer experiences, with Virtual Closet already driving 2x higher conversion and AskNykaa, our conversational search engine, emerging as a trusted beauty advisor on the platform. We remain focused on building with discipline, innovation, and long-term value creation,” Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa, said.

input.title: Nykaa Q1: Profit jumps over 3.2x YoY to Rs 80 crore, revenue up 29%
input.content:
Fashion-to-beauty retailer Nykaa on August 4 posted an over three-fold jump in quarterly profit to Rs 79.76 crore in the first quarter (Q1) of financial year 2026-25 (FY27), up from Rs 24.47 crore in the same period a year ago.
Sequentially, profit after tax remained largely flat. The Mumbai-based firm had reported a profit of Rs 78 crore in the previous quarter.
Gross profit rose 33 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,276 crore, while EBITDA increased 68 percent to Rs 236 crore. EBITDA margin expanded to 8.5 percent from 6.5 percent a year ago, marking its highest level in the last 12 quarters.
Nykaa’s revenue from operations rose 29 percent YoY to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1, up from Rs 2,155 crore a year ago. It had reported a revenue of Rs 2,648 crore in the previous quarter.
Total expenses for the firm came in at Rs 2,662.15 crore during the June quarter, up from Rs 2,120.56 crore a year ago and Rs 2,535.80 crore a quarter ago.
"This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters. Our platform featured exciting new brand launches like Rare beauty, one of the world’s largest celebrity beauty brands, already among the top 5 premium brands at Nykaa, SK-II, a Japanese high efficacy brand, and Judydoll, among our first Chinese beauty brands which is witnessing strong early traction among consumers," said Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa.
Our AI-led initiatives are beginning to create meaningful consumer experiences, with Virtual Closet already driving 2x higher conversion and AskNykaa, our conversational search engine, emerging as a trusted beauty advisor on the platform. We remain focused on building with discipline, innovation, and long-term value creation," she added.
Operationally, Nykaa's fashion business continued to outpace beauty, with fashion GMV rising 53 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,471 crore and net sales value (NSV) increasing 54 percent to Rs 451 crore. The business turned EBITDA margin positive at 0.1 percent, compared with a negative 6.2 percent in the year-ago quarter. The beauty vertical, meanwhile, delivered 29 percent NSV growth, supported by premium brand launches and retail expansion.
The company said it continued expanding its omnichannel presence during the quarter, taking its beauty retail network to 324 stores across 105 cities, while total retail space increased 29 percent year-on-year to 3.3 lakh sq ft. Its quick-commerce service Nykaa Now has expanded to 13 cities and is expected to reach more than 25 cities by the end of FY27.
Nykaa also said its owned brands portfolio continued to gain traction, reaching an annualised GMV run rate of around Rs 3,758 crore. The portfolio, which includes brands such as Kay Beauty and Dot & Key, grew NSV 36 percent year-on-year to Rs 550 crore during the quarter.
Nykaa’s Board of Directors also approved the acquisition of 51 percent shareholding on a fully diluted basis in skincare brand Aminu Wellness for a consideration of up to Rs 32 crores.
On August 4, Nykaa shares closed 0.85 percent higher on the BSE at Rs 344.80 apiece.

input.title: How Nykaa is building an owned-media empire
input.content:
ADVERTISEMENT
For most retailers, advertising is a cost centre. For Nykaa, it is increasingly becoming the product itself. Nykaa has assembled one of India's largest consumer-media ecosystems, with an audience that rivals some of the country's biggest digital publishers.
The numbers tell the story. Nykaa's beauty platform attracted 1.89 billion visits in FY26, drew 44.7 million monthly average unique visitors and served 19.7 million annual transacting customers. Its cumulative customer base has crossed 55 million, growing 31% year-on-year.
At that scale, Nykaa is no longer merely an e-commerce marketplace selling lipstick, skincare and fragrances. It is becoming an owned-media company with commerce attached.
Also read: Nykaa partners OpenAI to bring beauty, fashion catalogue into ChatGPT
From shelf space to screen space
Traditionally, beauty brands paid retailers for physical shelf space.
Today, they are paying for attention.
The company constantly refers to the intersection of commerce, content and community—a signal that content is no longer an ancillary function but a core growth engine.
Nykaa's influence extends far beyond transactions. Every product review, tutorial, influencer collaboration and recommendation creates media inventory that brands can tap into.
For global beauty players entering India, Nykaa increasingly offers distribution and access to millions of engaged consumers.
The audience is becoming the moat
Nykaa's business model is beginning to resemble that of a digital publisher.
The company added more than 200 beauty brands in FY26, including luxury labels such as Chanel Beauty, Armani Beauty, Kylie Cosmetics and SK-II. Overall, the platform now hosts more than 10,000 brands across beauty and fashion.
But unlike traditional retailers, Nykaa owns the consumer relationship.
It knows what consumers search for, what they buy, which creators they follow, what trends they engage with and how often they return.
That data advantage is transforming the company into a media platform capable of selling not just products, but discovery itself.
The rise of beauty intellectual property
Nykaa is investing heavily in proprietary experiences that look less like marketing campaigns and more like media franchises.
Properties such as Nykaaland, Nykaa Beauty Awards, Nykaa Luxe Weekender, Get Ready With Nykaa and Nykaa Academy are designed to keep consumers engaged long after a purchase.
These initiatives reveal a fundamental shift in marketing philosophy.
Traditional retailers spend on advertising to drive transactions. Nykaa is building intellectual property that generates recurring attention, engagement and loyalty.
The objective is not simply to sell products; it is to own the cultural conversation around beauty.
Read: Nykaa appoints Ankit Jain to lead quick commerce vertical NYKAA NOW
Creators are replacing commercials
For decades, beauty advertising in India was dominated by television campaigns and celebrity endorsements.
Nykaa is betting on a different future—one powered by creators, communities and experiences.
The company says it is deepening engagement with younger consumers through campus ambassador programmes, experiential activations and community-led initiatives. Consumer discovery is increasingly taking place on Instagram reels, YouTube tutorials and influencer content rather than in front of television screens.
That changes the economics of advertising.
Media budgets are moving away from thirty-second commercials towards creator partnerships, social commerce and immersive experiences.
In the next decade of beauty, the companies that win may not be the ones with the most products. They may be the ones that own the audience.

input.title: Sun Pharma maintains FY27 growth outlook, says Organon deal remains on track
input.content:
5 Min Read
Mumbai-based Sun Pharmaceutical Industries remains confident of delivering high single-digit revenue growth of 6-9% in FY27, with its innovative medicines portfolio, specialty business and new product launches expected to support growth.
Jayashree Satagopan, Chief Financial Officer of Sun Pharma, said it is too early to assess the potential impact of proposed US tariffs on generic medicines, noting that the company will continue engaging with the US administration and industry stakeholders.
She added that Sun Pharma's existing manufacturing footprint in the US provides strategic flexibility should policy changes materialise.
Satagopan also said the proposed Organon acquisition remains on track for completion in the last quarter of the current financial year, subject to regulatory approvals.
On the outlook for its innovative medicines business in FY27, Sun Pharma said it remains focused on expanding the portfolio, although it did not provide a specific growth target. The company expects products launched late last year to make a stronger contribution this year, while noting that growth will vary across markets depending on local dynamics.
In the April-June quarter (Q1FY27), Sun Pharma reported revenue of ₹15,299 crore, net profit of ₹2,894 crore, and a margin of 28.90%.
These are edited excerpts from the interview.Q: The company has maintained its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 6-9%, despite delivering 10% growth this quarter.
A: For the full year, we expect revenue growth to remain in the 6-9% range. One should also factor in the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations. We have seen rupee depreciation compared with last year, and that should be considered while evaluating the full-year performance.
A: We do not provide specific margin guidance. However, our endeavour is always to maximise margins to their fullest potential.
Q: What is the latest update on the Organon acquisition? Shareholders have approved it. Is the transaction still expected to close by early 2027?
A: Yes. Shareholders approved the transaction at their meeting on July 23. All the required regulatory filings across several countries have been completed. We remain on track to receive the approvals in a timely manner, and the last quarter of this financial year remains our target for closing the transaction.
Q: The US is debating tariffs on generic drugs and onshoring pharmaceutical manufacturing. How do you assess this as a risk to Sun Pharma?
A: The announcement came about a week ago regarding the additional tariffs that could be imposed on generics, possibly a couple of years from now. We need to assess the likely impact. There is still a long time between now and then. Sun Pharma will be engaging with the administration independently and along with our partners in the pharma industry. In my view, it is a little too early to comment on it. At the same time, we do have manufacturing facilities in the US for both technical operations and formulations, so we will evaluate the situation at the appropriate time.
Q: How does the Organon portfolio fit into the company's US strategy? Does its manufacturing presence help offset tariff concerns?
A: Organon's manufacturing is primarily in Europe and countries like Brazil and Mexico, not in the US. Therefore, the recent tariff announcement is unlikely to provide any benefit. Having said that, in the US, primarily they are into innovative medicines in the women's healthcare segment and biosimilars. These are complementary to Sun's existing portfolio.
Q: What about Organon's portfolio itself being impacted by Trump's policies on branded drugs and the most-favoured-nation pricing proposal?
A: Organon is still a separate listed company, so we are not in a position to comment on it at this point.
Q: How did the base generics business perform in the US, considering pricing pressure and the absence of Revlimid generic sales? What is the outlook?
A: One of the reasons the US generics business declined this quarter was the absence of Revlimid-related revenue. We launched five new generic products in the US and will continue introducing more products in that market. Pricing pressure remains a reality in the generics business and is expected to continue. We have seen this trend over the past few years, and we do not expect it to change in the coming quarters. Our focus is to introduce newer products while continuing to grow our innovative medicines business in the US.
Q: How did the global innovative medicines portfolio perform? What was the performance of drugs such as Unloxcyt and Leqselvi?
A: The overall business grew 12.8%, driven by both the US and international markets. We launched Leqselvi and Unloxcyt in the US, and both are tracking well in terms of formulary access and prescriptions. Prescriber feedback has been positive, and patient response, particularly for Leqselvi, has been encouraging. As of June 2026, Leqselvi had crossed 1,000 prescriptions. Unloxcyt is also progressing well. Since this is the first year of launch, we expect these products to continue gaining momentum over the coming months and quarters.
Q: Levulan saw an impact during the quarter. What happened?
A: It was a seasonal impact. The decline was quarter-on-quarter rather than year-on-year. Compared with the March quarter, the June quarter saw a slight decline, which is a normal seasonal trend.
Q: What is your outlook for the innovative medicines business in FY27?
A: While I cannot provide a specific growth percentage, our objective is to continue growing the innovative medicines portfolio. Different markets have different dynamics. We also have two products that were launched late last year, and they should contribute more meaningfully this year.

input.title: Sun Pharma to Thermax: 10 stocks Motilal Oswal is buying, selling and neutral on post Q1 results
input.content:
2/11
Sun Pharma beats estimates as global business booms
Sun Pharma just posted profits that blew past expectations, driven by strong other income and a global specialty portfolio growing at 13% a year. Now making up nearly a quarter of quarterly sales, this international push is becoming the company's real growth engine. The catch: US generic sales dipped due to tougher competition and one fading blockbuster drug. But India business is firing on all cylinders, thanks to aggressive brand-building and a bigger sales team. Analysts are staying bullish, expecting steady double-digit profit growth over the next two years.
Rating: Buy | Target Price: INR 2,310 (CMP: INR 1,991, +16% upside)
Getty Images
3/11
Maruti Suzuki's profit dips, but the real story is ahead
Maruti Suzuki's profits slipped about 11% this quarter as raw material costs squeezed margins harder than expected. But don't write off India's biggest carmaker just yet. Two upcoming price hikes and cooling commodity costs are set to repair those margins in the coming months. A packed new-model pipeline, low inventory levels, and two brand-new factories ramping up production all point to a stronger back half of the year. Analysts still expect a healthy earnings recovery over the next two years, betting this quarter's dip is just a temporary speed bump.
Rating: Buy | Target Price: INR 17,064 (CMP: INR 14,234, +20% upside)
Getty Images
4/11
ITC's cigarette business takes a hit from tax hikes
Smokers are feeling the pinch, and so is ITC. A sharp tax increase forced the cigarette giant into a slow, calibrated round of price hikes instead of passing on costs immediately, and it's costing them. Cigarette revenue fell over 20% this quarter, dragging overall profits down sharply. The bright spot: ITC's FMCG business is thriving, growing in double digits with improving profit margins. The company has even rolled out 30 new products to fight back against illegal cigarette competition. Analysts expect the pain in tobacco to continue for a few more quarters before things stabilize.
Rating: Neutral | Target Price: INR 300 (CMP: INR 281, +7% upside)
Getty Images
5/11
Bajaj Finserv gets an upgrade as insurance arm shines
Bajaj Finserv just earned a rare vote of confidence, an upgrade to a buy rating, after a standout quarter across its businesses. Revenue jumped nearly 20%, but the real headline is the life insurance arm, where the value of new business surged an impressive 87% year-on-year, far outpacing expectations. The general insurance unit also grew steadily, even as it waits for the motor insurance segment to pick back up. With profitability improving across the board and new ventures inching toward breakeven, analysts see a meaningful upside ahead for this financial services powerhouse.
Rating: Upgraded to Buy | Target Price: INR 2,490 (CMP: INR 2,029, +23% upside)
Getty Images
6/11
Tata Steel holds steady as India business roars
Tata Steel delivered a steady quarter, powered almost entirely by its India operations, where strong prices and controlled costs kept profits humming. The European business remains a drag, hovering near breakeven due to soft demand and operational headwinds — though analysts expect improving prices and efficiency gains to help turn that around in coming quarters. Near-term uncertainty around pricing and emissions rules in Europe hasn't dented the long-term outlook. With the stock trading at attractive valuations, analysts continue to recommend buying in, backed by India's continued strength.
Rating: Buy | Target Price: INR 220 (CMP: INR 190, +16% upside)
Getty Images
7/11
Divi's Labs crushes estimates with best margins in 5 years
Divi's Laboratories just delivered one of its strongest quarters in recent memory, smashing profit estimates by a stunning 37%. The secret? Its highest gross margins in 20 quarters, fueled by booming demand for custom drug manufacturing and a favorable currency environment. Major capacity expansion projects are nearing completion, and the company's growing peptide manufacturing business is shaping up as a key long-term growth driver. Analysts have raised their earnings forecasts in response, though with the stock already pricing in much of this optimism, they're staying cautiously neutral rather than turning outright bullish.
Rating: Neutral | Target Price: INR 7,720 (CMP: INR 8,056, -4% downside)
Getty Images
8/11
IOCL's surprise profit beat hides a bigger warning
Indian Oil Corporation stunned the market with a much smaller loss than analysts feared, thanks largely to one-time inventory gains worth over INR150 billion. Strip that out, and the underlying picture is tougher: massive losses on subsidized cooking gas cylinders, rising debt, and fuel margins under pressure from a spike in crude oil prices amid renewed geopolitical tensions. On the positive side, fuel demand is growing steadily and refining efficiency hit an all-time high. With several mega refinery projects nearing completion by year-end, analysts are holding a neutral stance while watching government support measures closely.
Rating: Neutral | Target Price: INR 150 (CMP: INR 140, +7% upside)
Getty Images
9/11
ABB India's orders surge, but margins stay a worry
ABB India delivered a quarter of contrasts, revenue and profit both beat expectations, but margins remain under pressure. New orders jumped an impressive 50%, pushing the total order book up 22%, largely driven by booming demand from data centers and electrification projects. That strong order momentum should support revenue growth ahead, but rising raw material and currency costs continue to squeeze profitability. With the stock already trading at a premium valuation near 91 times earnings, analysts are staying neutral, preferring to wait for margins to catch up with the growth story.
Rating: Neutral | Target Price: INR 6,700 (CMP: INR 7,285, -8% downside)
Getty Images
10/11
Muthoot Finance faces a gold loan price war
India's gold loan market is heating up — and not in a good way for Muthoot Finance. Margins fell sharply this quarter as competition from bigger, well-funded rivals intensified, forcing Muthoot to cut pricing just to protect its market share. While management expects lending rates to stabilize soon, analysts see real risk of continued pressure as more players chase the same booming gold loan demand. The company is now expected to grow its loan book by around 22% this year, but profit growth is projected to slow to just single digits, prompting a cautious neutral stance from analysts.
Rating: Neutral | Target Price: INR 2,850 (CMP: INR 3,120, -9% downside)
Getty Images
11/11
Thermax tumbles on cost overruns; analysts say sell
Thermax just delivered one of the weakest results of the season, missing estimates by a wide margin after a costly overrun on a major industrial project. The silver lining: that troubled legacy order book is set to wind down by early next year, which should help margins recover. The company's order pipeline still looks healthy, spanning clean energy, waste-to-energy, power plants, and even data center projects from the US. But with the stock trading at rich valuations despite the recent stumble, analysts have cut their earnings forecasts and are recommending investors sell.
Rating: Sell | Target Price: INR 4,000 (CMP: INR 4,306, -7% downside)

input.title: Sun Pharma recalls six eye drop brands from the Indian market as ‘precautionary measure’
input.content:
Sun Pharma recalls six eye drop brands from the Indian market as ‘precautionary measure’
The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. In a communication to its distributors, the company said the recall was “a precautionary measure”.
Synopsis: Sun Pharma has withdrawn six prescription eye drop brands from the Indian market and asked distributors to stop billing the products and return existing stocks. The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. The medicines are widely prescribed after eye surgery, particularly cataract procedures, to treat pain and inflammation.
Sun Pharma, the Mumbai-based pharma giant, has withdrawn six prescription eye drop brands from the Indian market. The recalled products are Nepalact OD, Nepalact, Nepalact-Z, Lotepred T, Lotepred LS and Lotepred 1%.
The drugs are routinely prescribed after eye surgery, particularly cataract procedures, which are among the most commonly performed surgeries in the country.
In a communication to its distributors, the company said the recall was “a precautionary measure” and instructed them to immediately cease billing the medicines, share details of existing inventory, and return all available stock, including products sourced through other channels.
The company has not disclosed the reason for the withdrawal. Its communication to distributors does not specify whether the action stems from a quality issue, a manufacturing concern, a regulatory requirement or another reason.
South First emailed Sun Pharma a detailed questionnaire seeking clarification on the withdrawal. The company had not responded at the time of publication.
Nepafenac and loteprednol are prescription medicines that require medical supervision.
The Nepalact range is generally prescribed to control pain and inflammation after cataract surgery. It contains nepafenac, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) formulated as an ophthalmic suspension.
“Patients usually begin using the drops a day before surgery and continue treatment for two to three weeks afterwards, depending on the surgeon’s advice,” an ophthalmologist told South First.
They added that nepafenac is also prescribed to prevent and treat macular oedema after cataract surgery, especially in patients with diabetes, who face a higher risk of the complication.
The Lotepred range contains loteprednol etabonate, a corticosteroid used to suppress inflammation after eye surgery and in several inflammatory eye disorders.
“Loteprednol is commonly used after cataract and refractive surgeries, as well as in conditions such as uveitis and allergic conjunctivitis. The drops are usually prescribed several times a day for one to two weeks after surgery, with the dosage gradually reduced as inflammation improves,” the ophthalmologist said.
Lotepred T, in particular, combines loteprednol with tobramycin, an antibiotic, allowing doctors to treat inflammation while also providing antibacterial cover where required.
The formulations differ in steroid strength. Lotepred LS contains a lower concentration suitable for milder inflammation, while Lotepred 1% is reserved for more severe cases, enabling ophthalmologists to tailor treatment to individual patients.
“Steroid eye drops such as loteprednol can increase intraocular pressure if used for prolonged periods. Because of this, ophthalmologists periodically monitor eye pressure during treatment to reduce the risk of complications such as glaucoma,” the ophthalmologist said.

input.title: Check your medicine cabinet: Sun Pharma recalls 10 eye drop brands over contamination concerns
input.content:
According to the letter, the affected products are Depopred2ML, Brinolar (BKC FREE), Brinzotim Eye Drops 5ML BKC FREE, Lotepred-5ML, Lotepred 1% Eye Drops SML, Lotepred LS 0.2% E/D 5ML, Lotepred T, Nepalact OD Eye Drops 3ML, Nepalact-Z, Toba-F and Nepalact E/D 5ML.
In the letter, the company said, "Sun Pharma Distributors Ltd has decided, as a precautionary measure, to discontinue further distribution [of], and withdraw all existing stocks of the above products available in your channel."
The company also asked distributors to stop billing the affected products immediately and share details of any stock they still have. The letter states, "In this regard, you are requested to immediately cease billing of the above-mentioned product and provide us details of any stock currently held by you."

It also asked distributors to return all available stock at the earliest. The letter added, "Further, you are requested to send back to us any stocks of the product available with you as well as those received from any sources on priority."
Responding to ANI, a Sun Pharma spokesperson said, "Patient safety remains our highest priority. We have taken all necessary steps in the best interest of patients and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. Our teams are working diligently to restore the availability of these products so that patients continue to have access to these treatment options."
An eye care expert said many of the recalled products are prescribed for patients recovering from eye surgery or treating long-term eye conditions such as glaucoma, eye infections, allergies and eye inflammation. "Many of these eye drops are prescribed for patients recovering from eye surgery or managing chronic conditions such as glaucoma, eye infections, allergies, and ocular inflammation, where interruption of treatment can have significant consequences," the expert said.
The expert also stressed the importance of maintaining sterility during manufacturing. "In a country like India, where millions rely on eye drops every day, maintaining sterility during manufacturing is non-negotiable. Even suspected contamination at a manufacturing facility can pose a serious risk to patient safety, making immediate product recalls essential," the expert said.
The expert advised patients not to stop using the recalled eye drops on their own. "Patients should not continue using a recalled product or discontinue treatment on their own, but should contact their ophthalmologist promptly so that an appropriate alternative can be prescribed, ensuring continuity of care while safeguarding vision," the expert said.

input.title: Falguni Nayar started Nykaa at 49: The entrepreneurial lesson every mid-career professional needs to hear
input.content:
There's a quiet kind of pressure that builds up somewhere around your late 40s. You've built a career, you've earned your stripes, and somewhere in the back of your mind sits a dream you never got around to chasing.
Most people file that dream away as "maybe in another life." Falguni Nayar didn't.
Nayar holds a commerce degree from Sydenham College, followed by an MBA from the prestigious IIM Ahmedabad.In 2012, after spending close to two decades she eventually walked away from banking to start Nykaa, a beauty and lifestyle platform built out of her father's spare office space.
Her story isn't really about beauty products. It's about what happens when someone refuses to let a number decide what they're capable of. Here are four lessons from her journey that every mid-career professional should sit with.
Experience is not baggage: It's your unfair advantage
For twenty years, Nayar sat across the table from India's most ambitious founders, valuing their companies and helping them go public.When she finally built something of her own, she wasn't fumbling in the dark the way a 25-year-old first-timer might. She understood capital, she understood scale, and she understood how investors think, because she'd been on their side of the table for two decades.
The lesson here is simple: the years you've spent in a "regular" job aren't wasted time. They're training you've already paid for.
Bold ambition, ethical execution
âOne of our biggest values is to be bold but good; it enables our employees to dream big but also do the right things in the right way, not taking any shortcuts for success,â Nayar said as reported by Business Today.
The quality this reflects is principled ambition, the discipline to chase growth without compromising integrity.Nykaaâs philosophy is that scale and ethics are not trade-offs, but partners; big dreams donât count unless they are built the right way.
This mindset encourages teams to take calculated risks, innovate boldly and still hold themselves accountable to fair processes and honest outcomes. It rejects the "growth at any cost" mentality common in fast-scaling businesses, instead embedding integrity into decision-making at every level.
Bet on people, not just on the plan
One of the more underrated parts of Nayar's playbook was her willingness to hire outside the obvious mould; bringing in leaders who had no prior background in beauty or personal care at all.
âSometimes you have to give people a chance. I bet on myself and everyone," said Nayar as Forbes reported.
Building something big at times can mean trusting people over pedigree.
Let go of what "supposed to" looks like
Nayar has said herself that entrepreneurship demands courage, and that age and experience are strengths, not liabilities.
She had to push back against the quiet assumption that a person past fifty had missed the window, and she did it not by arguing, but by simply building something that worked.
That's really the heart of her story; not that she ignored the doubt, but that she let her results speak instead of defending herself.
If there's one thing to take away from Falguni Nayar's journey, it's this: your career so far isn't a countdown clock. It might just be the runway you needed all along.

input.title: Sun Pharma Distributors Withdraws Several Eye Drops As Precautionary Measure
input.content:
Sun Pharma Distributors Withdraws Several Eye Drops As Precautionary Measure
Summarized by AI; it may make mistakes. Check important info
Sun Pharma Distributors Ltd has issued a confidential communication to distributors directing them to stop further distribution and withdraw existing stocks of several eye-drop products as a precautionary measure.
A copy of the letter dated July 17, accessed by ANI, lists products including Depopred 2ML, Brinolar (BKC Free), Brinzotim Eye Drops 5ML BKC Free, Lotepred-5ML, Lotepred 1% Eye Drops 5ML, Lotepred LS 0.2% E/D 5ML, Lotepred T, Nepalact OD Eye Drops 3ML, Nepalact-Z, Toba-F and Nepalact E/D 5ML.
Distributors Told To Return Stocks
The company has asked distributors to immediately cease billing for the listed products and provide details of any stocks currently in their possession.
It has also directed them to return all available stocks, including products received through other sources, on priority.
The communication describes the move as a precautionary withdrawal of the products from distribution channels.
Sun Pharma Says Patient Safety Is Priority
Responding to a local media, a Sun Pharma spokesperson said patient safety remained the company's highest priority.
"Patient safety remains our highest priority. We have taken all necessary steps in the best interest of patients and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements," the spokesperson said.
The company said its teams were working to restore availability of the products so that patients could continue to access the treatment options.
Expert Urges Patients Not To Stop Treatment On Their Own
A senior expert said several of the listed eye drops are used by patients recovering from eye surgery or managing conditions such as glaucoma, eye infections, allergies and ocular inflammation.
The expert said maintaining sterility during the manufacture of ophthalmic products was essential because suspected contamination could pose a serious risk to patients.
Patients using a recalled product should not continue using it, but should also not discontinue prescribed treatment without medical advice, the expert said. They should contact their ophthalmologist promptly so that an appropriate alternative can be prescribed and treatment can continue safely.
The company has not, in the communication cited, publicly detailed the specific reason behind the precautionary withdrawal.

input.title: Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi tops 1000 prescribers in US; seasonal shifts hits Levulan
input.content:
- Pharma Industry
- 4 min read
Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi tops 1000 prescribers in US; seasonal shifts hits Levulan
                    Speaking to analysts post first quarter FY27 results, Richard Ascroft, CEO of Sun Pharma’s North America business, said, "We are seeing good momentum in Leqselvi." which crossed 1,000 prescribers in June and has gained coverage across most payer programmes in the US. However, seasonal factors affecting another derma drug Levulan Kerastick, weighed on sequential growth of the specialty portfolio.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        New Delhi: Sun Pharma’s specialty therapy for alopecia areata, Leqselvi (deuruxolitinib), has crossed 1,000 prescribers within a year of its commercial launch in the US. The drug also posted its strongest monthly performance in June 2026, since its debut.
“We are seeing good momentum in Leqselvi, in the month of June we surpassed 1000 prescribers and also delivered our strongest month since launch, indicating increased adoption and growing confidence in the brand,” Richard Ascroft, CEO, North America business, Sun Pharma told analyst post first quarter FY27 results.
“The therapy is now covered under most payer programmes across the US,” he added.
In Q1, Sun Pharma specialty sales increased by 12.8 per cent by $351 million, accounting for 21.9 per cent of its total revenue.
However, sequentially sales slipped from $354 million in Q4 FY26 as sales of its other dermatology asset, Levulan Kerastick, a therapy to treat actinic keratoses (scaly patches on the face), were impacted by seasonality, weighing on sequential growth of the specialty portfolio.
The US business remained under pressure, with sales declining 9.7 per cent to $427 million, below street expectations of $470–480 million. The company pointed to continued erosion of cancer drug lenalidomide and increased competition in certain unspecified products as key factors impacting performance.
Meanwhile, other portfolio products, including Ilumya, Cequa and Odomzo, maintained positive momentum, and management expects the portfolio to grow at a “healthy rate.”
Commenting on the company's other recent launch, Unloxcyt (cosibelimab-ipdl), an oncology-dermatology therapy, Ascroft said early feedback from oncologists and dermatologists has been positive, due to tis durable efficacy and favourable safety profile largely driven by driven by its differentiated mechanism of action,
He added that the therapy is being added to a growing number of formularies at cancer centres and integrated delivery networks.
Sun Pharma is working with cancer centre administrators and oncologists to secure formulary inclusion and wider availability of the therapy.
In the pivotal Phase II expansion cohort of patients with locally advanced CSCC, designed to evaluate long-term efficacy and safety outcomes, the therapy reported a 50 per cent objective response rate, with complete responses in 27 per cent of patients, according to data presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting in Chicago.
R&D expenses for the quarter were Rs 824 crore, of which 30 per cent was directed towards innovative medicines. This included the ongoing investigator-led trial for Leqselvi to support a potential label expansion for adolescents aged 12–18 years, aimed at increasing the eligible patient pool — a strategy also adopted by competitors such as Eli Lilly’s Olumiant (baricitinib).
“Both of these products —Leqselvi and Unloxcyt— are still relatively early in their growth curve. While we continue to see good growth across the rest of our specialty portfolio, it will take some time before we see a larger contribution from these assets,” Ascroft said.
For its in-licensed knee pain therapy Nidlegy, its supply partner Philogen has asubmitted an updated Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA).
Sun Pharma holds exclusive rights to commercialize the drug across Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. Under the agreement, the two companies will share post-commercialization profit on 50:50 basis..
The acquisition is expected to be completed in Q4 FY27, in line with the company’s previously guided timeline and and the integration management office is working on day-one preparedness.
The company markets two brands — Noveltreat for weight management and Sematrinity for Type 2 diabetes — and has received positive feedback for its auto-injector device, which it said offers a convenient and user-friendly way of administering the drug.
According to the latest industry estimates, the two brands have collectively racked up around Rs 13 crore from with net sales of 64,000 units since their launch in March.
“We have become the No. 2 player among generics, and our focus is to grow above the market and gain market share,” Kirti Ganorkar, MD, Sun Pharma said adding that, we see this as a very exciting opportunity and are well prepared to meet the demand, with established capabilities across API, formulation and delivery devices through both in-house capabilities and supplier partnerships
In Q1, the Mumbai-based drugmaker total sales stood at Rs 15,183 crore, up 10.1 per cent from a year earlier, while adjusted net profit rose marginally by 3.1 per cent to Rs 3,089 crore.
The net effective tax rate was 27.4 per cent, impacted by geographies with varying tax rates. Management expects the tax rate to remain at similar levels until the completion of the Organon transaction.

input.title: ChrysCapital Takes Control of Novartis India with Stake Acquisition
input.content:
Novartis India Ltd is set to enter a new phase of growth following the acquisition of the Swiss parent company’s 70.68% stake by private equity firm ChrysCapital. The transaction marks a significant ownership transition, paving the way for the company to adopt a new corporate identity, appoint a new leadership team and strengthen its presence in India’s branded pharmaceuticals market. The acquisition follows Novartis AG’s decision in 2024 to review the future of its India-listed subsidiary. Announced earlier this year, the deal was valued at ₹1,446 crore.
ChrysCapital Makes First Majority Investment in Indian Pharma
With this acquisition, ChrysCapital has made its first majority-controlled investment in India’s pharmaceutical sector. The private equity firm said Novartis India will adopt a new name and corporate identity, reflecting its transition from the Swiss pharmaceutical group to an independently managed company backed by private equity. ChrysCapital aims to transform the business into a leading branded generics platform for the Indian pharmaceutical market while building on the company’s strong legacy and established market presence.
New Leadership Team to Drive Next Growth Phase
As part of the ownership transition, Novartis India has appointed Dr. Vikas Gupta as Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director. The company has also strengthened its Board by appointing Ramesh Ramadurai, Suchita Sharma and Shashank Sinha as Independent Directors. Initially, the business will continue leveraging its existing contract manufacturing partnerships while gradually building its own operational capabilities.
Management Focuses on Portfolio Expansion
Dr. Vikas Gupta, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, said the company intends to build on its decades-long legacy of scientific excellence and physician confidence. He noted that, with ChrysCapital’s support, the company now has the resources and strategic focus to expand its product portfolio, reach more patients and accelerate long-term growth while preserving the values that have defined the organisation over the years.
ChrysCapital Sees Long-Term Value Creation
Kshitij Sheth, Managing Director at ChrysCapital Advisors, said the company’s established brands, strong market reputation and trusted legacy provide a solid foundation for sustainable long-term value creation. He added that ChrysCapital will work closely with the management team to unlock new growth opportunities and strengthen the company’s position in India’s rapidly evolving pharmaceutical market.
New Chapter Begins for Novartis India
With new ownership, experienced leadership and a planned corporate rebranding, Novartis India is poised to begin a new chapter focused on expanding its branded generics business. As reported by thehindubusinessline.com, backed by ChrysCapital’s investment and strategic direction, the company aims to leverage its legacy brands while pursuing sustainable growth in one of the world’s fastest-growing pharmaceutical markets.

input.title: Sun Pharma Q1 net rises 27% to ₹2,895 crore
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceuticals Industries Ltd. for the first quarter ended June 30, 2026 reported a 27% year-n-year growth in consolidated net profit to ₹2,895 crore.
Sales income at ₹15,184 crore grew 10.1%. Global Innovative Medicines sales at $351 million grew 12.8% accounting for 21.9% of sales.
Kirti Ganorkar, Managing Director, Sun Pharma said, “Our performance during the quarter was driven by strong momentum in India as well as Innovative Medicines, which delivered robust growth across the U.S. and international regions.”
“Recent semaglutide approvals in India, Brazil and South Africa underscore our capabilities in developing complex peptide products for patients globally. Organon shareholders have approved the proposed acquisition by Sun, which is on track to close in early 2027,” he added.
Formulation sales in India were ₹5,475 crore, registering a growth of 16%. India Formulation sales accounted for 36.1% of total consolidated sales, the company said.
Formulation sales in the U.S. were $427 million, lower by 9.7%. “Innovative Medicines continued to grow, partially offsetting the decline in generics business. U.S. sales accounted for approximately 26.6% of total consolidated sales,” the company said.
Emerging Markets formulations sales were $311 million, up by 4.2% and accounted for 19.4% of total consolidated sales.
Rest of World (ROW) Formulations sales were $218 million and accounted for 13.6% of total consolidated sales, the company said.
While Global Innovative Medicines sales were $351 million for Q1FY27, up 12.8% and accounted for 21.9% of sales, external sales of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) were ₹597 crore, up 10.5%.

input.title: Sun Pharma misses Q1 estimates as US generics drag offsets India growth
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, India's largest drugmaker market capitalization, missed Street expectations in the June quarter as weakness in its US generics business weighed on profitability despite double-digit revenue growth and continued strength in its India and innovative medicines businesses.
The company reported consolidated revenue of ₹15,299 crore for the June quarter, up 10.5% year-on-year, while net profit rose 27% to ₹2,895 crore. Strong growth in the domestic business and innovative medicines offset a decline in US generics sales but was not enough to meet analyst estimates.
A Bloomberg poll had pegged revenue at ₹15,527 crore and net profit at ₹2,974 crore.
Quick answers to key questions
Sun Pharma missed Q1 estimates primarily due to weakness in its US generics business, which affected overall profitability, even as it reported strong double-digit growth in its India and innovative medicines divisions.
Sun Pharma's domestic business saw a 16% year-on-year growth, contributing 36% of overall revenue, while its US generics sales fell 9.7% year-on-year due to pricing pressure and increased competition.
Innovative medicines are central to Sun Pharma's strategy, significantly driving growth, particularly in the US and emerging markets, where they recently reported a 12.8% year-on-year sales increase.
The US generics market is impacting Sun Pharma's profitability by introducing pricing pressures and intensifying competition, leading to a decline in generic sales that counteracts the company's otherwise strong performance.
Sun Pharma's overall revenue growth in Q1 can be attributed to strong performance in its domestic market and growth from innovative medicines, which helped offset the decline in US generics sales.
Adjusted net profit rose 3.1% to ₹3,089 crore. Ebitda increased 2.7% to ₹4,417 crore, while the Ebitda margin narrowed to 28.9% from 31.1% a year earlier. Management said on the post-earnings investor call that the year-on-year decline in margin reflected a high base, as the year-ago quarter had benefited from stronger sales of blood cancer drug lenalidomide in the U.S.
“Our performance during the quarter was driven by strong momentum in India as well as Innovative Medicines, which delivered robust growth across the U.S. and international regions,” managing director Kirti Ganorkar said in a statement.
Shares of the company closed 0.7% lower at ₹1,987 apiece on the National Stock Exchange on Friday.
Global innovative medicines sales rose 12.8% year-on-year to $351 million, accounting for 21.9% of total sales. In its investor presentation, the company said the innovative portfolio remains central to its strategy and continued to drive growth in both the US and emerging markets during the quarter.
India remained Sun Pharma's largest market, contributing 36% of overall revenue. Sales in the domestic business climbed 16% year-on-year to ₹5,475 crore, outpacing the broader Indian pharmaceutical market, which grew 12% during April-May 2026.
The US business, however, remained under pressure. Sales fell 9.7% year-on-year to $427 million as pricing pressure and rising competition eroded generic drug sales.
Growth from innovative medicines, including psoriasis treatment Ilumya, skin cancer drug Odomzo and chronic dry eye therapy Cequa, partly offset the decline. Generic products, including blood cancer drug lenalidomide, continued to weaken because of intensifying competition and pricing pressure.
“Recent semaglutide approvals in India, Brazil and South Africa underscore our capabilities in developing complex peptide products for patients globally,” Ganorkar said.
Sun Pharma holds the second-largest share of India's semaglutide market, Ganorkar told investors. The company has already commercialized the drug in South Africa after receiving approval last week and plans to launch it in Brazil following regulatory approval earlier this week.
“We are well prepared for the launches,” Ganorkar said, adding that the company has secured its supply chain to meet expected demand through in-house API manufacturing, formulation capabilities and partnerships with device manufacturers.
The company also said the acquisition of Organon, announced in April at an enterprise value of $11.75 billion, received shareholder approval on 23 July and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of the current fiscal year (FY27).
The emerging markets business, which includes countries like Romania, Brazil, South Africa and Mexico, recorded revenue of $311 million, 4.2% higher than last year, driven by innovative drugs. The business accounted for 19.4% of overall sales for the quarter.
Meanwhile growth remained flat in the rest of world (RoW) markets, including Western Europe, Canada, Japan, Australia and New Zealand, with revenue at $218 million.
